title: Prediction models for venous thromboembolism in pediatric patients: A protocol for systematic review and critical appraisal.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) in children is a severe disease with high mortality rates. It is also gradually recognized as a major source of morbidity in hospitalized children, leading to increased length of hospital stay, higher mortality, and increased costs. The majority of pediatric subjects with VTE present inherited or acquired risk factors,such as the use of a central venous catheter (CVC), which accounts for more than more than 90% of neonatal VTE and 50% of pediatric VTE. Clinical studies on predictive models for VTE in children have shown inconsistent results. This systematic review aims to evaluate published prediction models for pediatric VTE, analyzing their characteristics, predictors, efficacy, and the methodological quality and applicability. The protocol has been prepared using the Preferred Items for Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) guidelines. The systematic review protocol for VTE prediction in pediatric patients has been registered on PROSPERO (PROSPERO 2025CRD420251231316. Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/vi-ew/CRD420251231316.) A comprehensive search across five major databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang) will be conducted for studies on prediction models of VTE among pediatric patients. Two researchers will independently screen literature, extract data, and evaluate the bias risk and applicability of included studies using prediction modelling study tools. This systematic review will provide critical insights into the efficacy and quality of reporting of the VTE model in pediatric patients. This will guide clinical physicians in selecting the most appropriate VTE prediction model and inform future research endeavors in pediatric VTE prediction.

title: The Coagulation-Immune Axis in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Mechanisms, Prognostic Significance, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) develops in a microbe-rich, injury-prone mucosa in which coagulation, inflammation, and tissue repair are closely coupled. Tumor and host cells can activate tissue factor-thrombin signaling, platelets, fibrin turnover, extracellular vesicles, and neutrophil extracellular traps, thereby reshaping myeloid-cell recruitment, cytotoxic immunity, angiogenesis, and invasion. However, local procoagulant biology does not necessarily predict systemic venous thromboembolism. We therefore organize the evidence using a compartmentalized immunothrombosis model that distinguishes intratumoral coagulation-immune remodeling, systemic thrombosis, and treatment-dependent perioperative events. Direct OSCC studies support several components of this network, but much of the evidence linking coagulation to immune escape and treatment response remains preclinical or extrapolated from other tumors. Circulating D-dimer, fibrinogen, platelet indices, and inflammatory ratios show prognostic associations, yet their incremental value beyond established clinicopathologic factors has not been established. Anticoagulant, antiplatelet, protease-activated receptor, podoplanin-CLEC-2, fibrinolytic, and NET-directed strategies are biologically plausible but should not be used as OSCC treatment without a standard indication or clinical trial. Future studies should pair longitudinal blood measurements with spatial tumor profiling and match interventions to a verified mechanism, anatomical compartment, and safe treatment window.

title: The Lost Kidney: Ultrasound Diagnosis of Adult Bochdalek Hernia With Renal Herniation and Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: Adult Bochdalek hernia (BH) with left renal herniation is clinically rare and has an insidious onset, rendering it prone to misdiagnosis. We report a case of a 77-year-old male patient who presented with an abdominal pulsatile mass in the absence of respiratory symptoms. Ultrasonography revealed a giant abdominal aortic aneurysm and additionally identified renal echogenicity on the left side of the heart, with a normally positioned spleen. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated herniation of the left kidney and a portion of the bowel into the thoracic cavity, along with a giant abdominal aortic aneurysm and multiple atherosclerotic ulcers of the iliac arteries. Ultrasonography is valuable for initial screening, while contrast-enhanced CT defines diaphragmatic defect, ectopic-kidney rotational malformation, and elongated renal pedicle, providing critical evidence for definitive diagnosis.

title: Presentation, management, and outcomes of ectopic Cushing syndrome: an international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ectopic Cushing syndrome is a rare condition with scarce outcome data. We sought to characterise its course and determinants of complications and mortality. METHODS: In this international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study, 49 high-volume endocrine referral centres across Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and New Zealand identified consecutive eligible patients. We included patients with a clinical diagnosis of ectopic Cushing syndrome, defined by expert adjudication at the treating institution with at least one of the following criteria: inferior petrosal sinus sampling or dynamic testing supportive of ectopic Cushing syndrome, biochemical remission of hypercortisolism following treatment of the ectopic Cushing syndrome source (surgical excision, radiotherapy, or cryoablation), evidence of a non-metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome, either on initial or subsequent imaging, or evidence of a metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome either on imaging or from chart notes. Data collection was completed between May 31, 2024 and April 22, 2025. Clinical features, biochemical severity, management, complications, and mortality were assessed. The primary outcome was Cushing syndrome-related mortality (investigator-adjudicated). Secondary outcomes were overall mortality and incidence of complications. Outcomes were stratified based on biochemical remission and timeline since diagnosis. Early (within 6 months of diagnosis) and late (>6 months after diagnosis) outcomes were analysed using landmark methods. FINDINGS: Among 1463 patients (median age 51 years [IQR 37-64; range 3-87], 824 [56·3%] women, 639 [43·7%] men, and 1021 [69·8%] of White race), 836 (57·1%) had metastatic disease. Severe hypercortisolism (1204 [91·1%] of 1321) and hypokalaemia (1111 [79·4%] of 1399) were common. Median duration of follow-up was 57 months (IQR 19-124). Cushing syndrome-related death occurred in 196 (13·4%) patients. 626 (42·8%) patients died overall. Infection occurred in 464 (31·7%) patients, venous thromboembolism in 124 (8·5%), cardiovascular events in 93 (6·4%), and cerebrovascular events in 37 (2·5%). Achievement of complete biochemical remission within 6 months of diagnosis was independently associated with lower risk of late complications (adjusted HR 0·55 [95% CI 0·38-0·80]) and Cushing syndrome-related mortality (0·49 [0·27-0·89]), whereas no association was observed with non-Cushing syndrome-related mortality. INTERPRETATION: Outcomes in ectopic Cushing syndrome are driven by early control of hypercortisolism. Failure to achieve remission within 6 months is associated with markedly worse complications and mortality, supporting ectopic Cushing syndrome as a time-critical endocrine emergency. FUNDING: Mayo Clinic.

title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h.

title: Radiofrequency ablation with versus without high ligation for primary varicose veins of the great saphenous vein: A comparison of efficacy and outcomes.
abstract: p p p p p p p p p p PurposeThis study compares radiofrequency ablation (RFA) with versus without high ligation (HL) for treating primary varicose veins of the great saphenous vein, assessing differences in surgical efficacy.MethodIn this retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients with lower-extremity varicose veins treated at a single vascular center (July 2023-July 2024) were allocated to RFA (n = 65) or RFA ablation with high ligation (RFA + HL, n = 72). Groups were compared for operative time, blood loss, postoperative pain, hospital stay, symptom relief, and 2-year recanalization and recurrence rates.ResultsBoth RFA and RFA + HL demonstrated favorable therapeutic outcomes, with significant symptom improvement observed in all patients postoperatively. The RFA group demonstrated superior perioperative outcomes, including shorter operative time (60.46 ± 7.89 vs. 65.21 ± 8.28 min,= 0.001), less blood loss (11.92 ± 5.50 vs. 14.46 ± 6.94 mL,= 0.020), lower postoperative VAS scores at 1d and 3d (< 0.01), a shorter hospital stay (2.15 ± 0.67 vs. 2.39 ± 0.64 days,= 0.037), and a lower incidence of impaired wound healing (0.0% vs. 9.7%,= 0.014). In contrast, RFA + HL provided better long-term durability, with significantly lower recanalization rates at both 9-month (1.4% vs. 10.8%,= 0.027) and 12-month (2.8% vs. 12.3%,= 0.047) follow-ups, as well as at 18-month (2.8% vs. 13.8%,= 0.017) and 24-month (4.2% vs. 16.9%,= 0.014) follow-ups. Notably, by 24 months postoperatively, clinical recurrence had occurred in 6 patients (9.2%) in the RFA group but none in the RFA + HL group (= 0.010).ConclusionCompared with RFA alone, the combination of RFA and HL for treating GSV incompetence was associated with a longer operative time and a higher risk of incision-related complications in the groin. However, the combined procedure demonstrated a lower venous recanalization rate at the 1-year follow-up, suggesting superior long-term durability of GSV closure.

title: Association Between Hypoperfusion Intensity Ratio and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic utility of the hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR) in posterior circulation stroke is undefined. We investigated the association between pretreatment HIR and outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy for acute posterior circulation large vessel occlusion. METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION (Endovascular Treatment for Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion)/ATTENTION-IA (Intra-Arterial Tenecteplase After Successful Endovascular Recanalisation in Patients With Acute Posterior Circulation Arterial Occlusion) trials included patients with posterior circulation occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had baseline computed tomography perfusion. HIR (Tmax>10 s/ Tmax>6 s volume) was analyzed. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days was the primary outcome. RESULTS: P P Among 139 patients, higher HIR (per 0.1 increment) was independently associated with lower odds of 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 (adjusted odds ratio, 0.643 [95% CI, 0.422-0.979];=0.039). However, its discriminative ability was the modest (area under the curve, 0.617 [95% CI, 0.521-0.712]). The established anterior circulation cutoff (HIR<0.4) did not predict outcomes (=0.115). CONCLUSIONS: Elevated HIR is independently associated with worse 90-day outcomes after posterior circulation mechanical thrombectomy, but its overall prognostic utility is limited, and the anterior circulation threshold (0.4) could not be validated in this underpowered analysis, highlighting circulation-specific pathophysiological differences.

title: Association Between Blood Pressure Variability and Acute Kidney Injury Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Study Based on the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV Database.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Acute kidney injury (AKI) following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is a prevalent complication that impacts patient prognosis. While blood pressure variability (BPV) has been implicated in AKI among patients undergoing other surgical procedures, its association with AKI following TAVR remains uncharted. This study aimed to investigate the association between BPV and post-TAVR AKI. METHODS: Based on the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care database, logistic regression models were employed to investigate the associations of average real variability of systolic blood pressure (ARV-SBP) and average real variability of diastolic blood pressure (ARV-DBP) with AKI following TAVR. Multiple sensitivity analyses evaluated the robustness of the results. The marginal standardization analysis estimated the odds of AKI after ARV-SBP adjustment. RESULTS: A total of 340 patients undergoing TAVR were enrolled, among whom 107 (31.5%) developed AKI. Logistic regression analysis demonstrated a positive correlation between ARV-SBP and the odds of post-TAVR AKI (odds ratio [OR] = 1.34, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.03-1.74, P = .029) in the fully adjusted model. In contrast, no significant correlation was observed between ARV-DBP and AKI (P = .559). In covariate and blood pressure measurement sensitivity analyses, the direction of the ARV-SBP effect was generally consistent with that in the primary analysis. Marginal standardization analysis demonstrated that higher ARV-SBP levels were associated with elevated odds of AKI. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated ARV-SBP was associated with increased odds of post-TAVR AKI. Average real variability of systolic blood pressure may serve as an auxiliary indicator for early risk identification of post-TAVR AKI, yet its clinical value remains to be validated in prospective studies.

title: Clinical value of a five-predictor nomogram for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after orthopaedic surgery in ICU patients.
abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the predictive value of a five-predictor nomogram for postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in orthopedic patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU).MethodsClinical data from 224 postoperative orthopedic ICU patients admitted between March 2022 and March 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were divided into a DVT group (n = 73) and a non-DVT group (n = 151). Logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent risk factors, and a predictive nomogram was constructed based on these variables. The performance of the model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.ResultsThe incidence of postoperative DVT was 32.59%. Patients in the DVT group had significantly higher age, D-dimer, prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), and a higher prevalence of diabetes, preoperative heart failure, and postoperative infection compared with the non-DVT group (P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified age, diabetes, preoperative heart failure, PT, and APTT as independent risk factors for DVT. The nomogram demonstrated good predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.877. The sensitivity and specificity were 82.47% and 76.68%, respectively.ConclusionThe five-predictor nomogram provides individualized estimates of postoperative DVT probability in orthopedic ICU patients and may support risk stratification and targeted prevention.

title: 125 Endovascular brachytherapy usingI seeds strand combined with transarterial chemoembolization, lenvatinib, and camrelizumab for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma with hepatic vein tumor thrombus.
abstract: PURPOSE: 125 To evaluate the safety and efficacy of Iodine-125(I) seed strand implantation in combination with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), lenvatinib, and camrelizumab for the treatment of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) with hepatic vein tumor thrombus (HVTT). METHODS AND MATERIALS: 125 From January 2020 to December 2023, 76 uHCC patients with HVTT were included in this single-center retrospective study. Thirty-six patients underwentI seed strand implantation combined with TACE, lenvatinib, and camrelizumab (group A), whereas 40 patients received TACE combined with lenvatinib and camrelizumab (group B). Outcome measures comprised with technique success rate, overall response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), overall survival (OS) time, progression-free survival (PFS) time, and adverse event occurrence rate. RESULTS: 125 The technique was successfully performed in all patients. The mean intended dose (r, irradiation range = 10 mm; z, irradiation duration = 240 days) was 64.0 ± 0.3 Gy. No grade 3 or 4 adverse events related toI seed strand implantation occurred in group A. The ORR and DCR of HVTT were significantly higher in group A compared with group B (ORR, 72.2% vs. 15.0%, p < 0.001; DCR, 88.9% vs. 35%, p < 0.001). And the median OS time and PFS time were significant longer in group A compared with group B (OS, 22.1 ± 2.4 vs. 14.0 ± 1.7 months, p < 0.001; PFS, 17.6 ± 0.3 vs. 8.0 ± 0.6 months, p < 0.001). In the multivariate Cox regression analysis, treatment regimen was an independent prognostic factor for OS. No serious complications related to interventional treatment, including acute hepatic failure, liver abscess, intraperitoneal bleeding, and radiation hepatitis was observed. CONCLUSIONS: 125 I seeds strand combined with TACE, lenvatinib, and camrelizumab as the treatment strategy for uHCC patients with HVTT is safe and effective.

title: Orthoplastic Limb Salvage Using Transtibial Transport and Free-Flap Reconstruction in Patients With Diabetes-Related Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract: Early revascularization-through endovascular or open surgery-is the cornerstone of treatment for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, some patients are deemed "no-option" because of diffuse infrapopliteal disease, poor distal runoff, or failed previous interventions, leaving limited limb-salvage strategies. We report an orthoplastic limb-salvage case in a 56-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes, severe peripheral arterial disease, and a chronic foot ulcer complicated by toe gangrene after unsuccessful revascularization. After urgent radical débridement, ray amputation, culture-directed antibiotics, and negative-pressure wound therapy, transtibial transport (TTT) was done to improve microcirculation. After infection control and wound stabilization, definitive reconstruction was achieved using a large anterolateral thigh perforator free flap with a flow-through microsurgical technique to provide durable coverage while preserving distal perfusion. At 12-month follow-up, the flap remained viable with complete epithelialization, no ulcer recurrence, preserved foot architecture, and independent ambulation with protective footwear, indicating meaningful functional recovery. This case highlights the potential role of combining TTT with microsurgical reconstruction in orthoplastic management of "no-option" CLTI. Enhancing microcirculation alongside robust soft-tissue coverage may expand limb-salvage possibilities when traditional revascularization is not feasible.

title: Development and Validation of a Nomogram for Predicting Preoperative Venous Thromboembolism in Patients With Lower Extremity Fractures: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: p = BackgroundPatients with lower extremity fractures (LEF) are at high risk of preoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, existing risk assessment models are not specifically developed and validated for this population.ObjectiveTo develop and validate a prediction model for preoperative VTE in emergency LEF patients, and to compare the performance of traditional logistic regression (LR) with that of machine learning (ML) algorithms.DesignRetrospective cohort study.SettingPeking University Shenzhen Hospital, China.Participants486 patients with LEF admitted between January 2022 and July 2025.MethodsTwo modeling strategies were compared: 1) a traditional LR nomogram using backward stepwise selection, and 2) nine ML algorithms with Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO)-based feature selection. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination (area under the curve, AUC), calibration, classification metrics (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) and decision curve analysis.ResultsOf 486 enrolled patients, 79 (16.3%) developed preoperative VTE. Among the ML models, LASSO-LR and multilayer perceptron (MLP) achieved the highest validation AUCs (0.709 each), the best calibration and highest net benefit. The traditional LR nomogram showed an identical AUC of 0.709 (95% CI: 0.691-0.718), with superior calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow0.738, calibration intercept = -0.109, slope = 0.921) and better stability. Therefore, this simple five-predictor traditional LR nomogram, incorporating age ≥ 65 years, hemoglobin, glucose, external immobilization, and pre-injury anticoagulant or antiplatelet use, was selected as the optimal model.ConclusionThe traditional LR nomogram appears promising for preoperative VTE risk prediction in LEF patients. External validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: SERPINE1 IntegratingGenotype With Clinical Indicators Improves Venous Thromboembolism Risk Prediction in Cancer Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study From Xinjiang.
abstract: SERPINE1 SERPINC1 PROC MTHFR F5 F2 SERPINE1 P SERPINE1 ObjectiveTo develop and validate a venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk prediction model integrating genetic polymorphisms and routine clinical indicators in a cohort of cancer patients from Xinjiang, China.MethodsA retrospective study was conducted on 1135 cancer patients (179 with VTE, 956 without) at Affiliated Cancer Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University between March 2024 and May 2025. Six gene polymorphisms (,,,,,) and clinical predictors were assessed. Chi-square tests and logistic regression identified independent predictors for model construction. Model performance was evaluated using ROC analysis, and three clinically optimized cut-off values were defined.ResultsThe4G allele was identified as a strong genetic risk factor for VTE (4G/4G genotype: OR=2.330, 95%CI: 1.378-3.942; 4G/5G genotype: OR=2.399, 95%CI: 1.411-4.078). No significant associations were found for the other five genes. Age (OR=1.022, 95%CI: 1.008-1.037), D-dimer level (OR=1.288, 95%CI: 1.186-1.399), and hemoglobin level (OR=0.987, 95%CI: 0.979-0.995) were independent clinical predictors (<0.01). The combined model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.769 (95%CI: 0.731-0.807). Three optimized cut-off values were derived for different clinical contexts: high-sensitivity (90.5%), balanced (Youden index 0.434), and high-specificity (90.1%).ConclusionThe4G allele independently predicts VTE risk in this cohort of cancer patients from Xinjiang. A prediction model integrating this genetic marker with age, D-dimer, and hemoglobin demonstrates good discriminatory performance. The three derived cut-off values may facilitate risk-stratified thromboprophylaxis in clinical practice; however, these findings are based on a retrospective, single-center cohort and internally validated only by ROC analysis.

title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

title: An anatomy-aware spatio-temporal generative extrapolation network for distal ascending aorta restoration in standard echocardiographic views.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), the standard parasternal long-axis (PLAX) view enables reliable evaluation of the aortic valve and aortic root. Owing to the limited field of view of the ultrasound probe and rib-window occlusion, the distal ascending aorta (AA) is frequently truncated, compromising the diagnosis of aortic aneurysm and dilation. PURPOSE: We aim to address the incomplete visualization of the distal AA in standard PLAX views. By aggregating fragmented anatomical features intermittently visible in adjacent frames, we enhance the clarity of vessel wall edges and generate the distal AA structure, thereby completing the missing AA imagery in standard PLAX views. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ± Δ = 0.2 cm We retrospectively collected 1160 TTE videos from Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital (August 2022 - December 2024), all showing complete AA anatomy. After de-identification, 1059 cases were randomly split into training/validation/test sets (6:2:2), and 101 cases were reserved for observer agreement experiments. An additional 152 videos from three different device models (EPIQ CVX, GE Voluson E10, Resona A20T) formed an external validation set. Two training data types were constructed: (i) dual-view synchronous data - a standard PLAX sequence and an AO-PLAX sequence acquired after a cranial probe shift, phase-matched at end diastole (ED); and (ii) locally masked data - the distal AA region was masked, forcing the model to infer missing anatomy from left-side context. Input sequences of five frames (ED2) were extracted. The proposed Spatio-Temporal Ascending-Aorta generative adversarial network (STAA-GAN) first aligns adjacent frames using an Edge Boosted Feature Alignment (EBFA) module with multi-stage modulated deformable convolutions. A channel-wise fusion strategy then aggregates temporally aligned features. The fused representation is fed into a Swin-UNet generator enhanced with a Strip based Cross window Prediction (SCP) module to capture long-range structural dependencies. Training employs a composite loss including pixel reconstruction, feature reconstruction, texture consistency, relativistic average least-squares GAN (RaLSGAN), temporal coherence, and structure-aware terms, with data-dependent weighting. Statistical analyzes included Bland-Altman, Passing-Bablok regression, paired t-tests with Cohen's d, Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, and two one-sided tests (TOST,). RESULTS: α 1 = 0.00417 ≤ 0.01 ± 0.13 Δ = 0.2 p < 0.001 0.913 0.045 ± p < 0.001 d < 0.2 STAA-GAN achieved the best image-quality values among the compared methods, with peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) = 22.51 dB, structural similarity index (SSIM) = 0.7574, multi-scale structural similarity index (MS-SSIM) = 0.8598, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) = 0.1758. All 12 pairwise comparisons (SRN, IOH, and U-Transformer versus STAA-GAN, designated as the reference group) remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (), with absolute effect sizes ranging from 0.255 to 3.439. The per-frame inference time was 203 ms. In clinical consistency validation, the mean difference between measurements on generated and original images was cm with 95% limits of agreement within cm; TOST with cm confirmed clinical equivalence for all comparisons (). The segmentation Dice coefficient on generated images averagedacross five cross-validation folds. External validation on three different ultrasound devices (Philips, GE, Mindray) maintained consistent equivalence (TOST, Cohen's). These results demonstrate that STAA-GAN produces clinically interchangeable distal ascending aorta images with high fidelity and real-time feasibility. CONCLUSIONS: STAA-GAN enables extrapolation of the missing distal ascending aorta in standard PLAX views, achieving improved image quality and clinically equivalent diameter measurements on both internal and external validation datasets. These findings support its potential for assisting distal ascending aorta assessment in routine echocardiography.

PURPOSE: We aim to address the incomplete visualization of the distal AA in standard PLAX views.

title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention. AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement. STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool. RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps. CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

title: Three working windows posterior midline approach for posterior column tibial plateau fractures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures with combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression are challenging because conventional posterior approaches limit instrument trajectories and reduction vectors for distinct posterior fragments. METHODS: Ten patients with isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures accompanied by combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression were treated using a posterior midline skin incision organized into three working windows. The central window served as the foundational posterior corridor, with medial and lateral windows developed as functional extensions to facilitate region-specific reduction and fixation. Relevant clinical data and outcomes were retrospectively analyzed. RESULTS: Postoperative radiographs of all 10 patients showed satisfactory joint reduction and alignment. Radiographic fracture union was achieved in all cases at a mean of 13.9 weeks, with a mean follow up of 11.8 months. At final follow up, mean knee flexion was 124.0°, and mean knee extension was -2.1°, and the mean Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) knee score was 90.8 points. One patient developed a superficial wound infection that resolved with antibiotic treatment, and one patient experienced deep vein thrombosis that was successfully treated with anticoagulation therapy. No neurovascular injuries, deep infections, or fixation failures were observed during follow up. CONCLUSION: A posterior midline approach organized into three working windows may provide a feasible option for selected isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures with combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression, allowing region-specific posterior fixation through a single posterior skin incision.

title: Underdetected peripheral artery disease in people with hypertension: A narrative review of risk-stratified case-finding, diagnostic pathways, and equity in care.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common but often underrecognized in people with hypertension because symptoms are frequently absent or atypical and access to physiologic testing is uneven. This narrative review examines how hypertension care can support risk-stratified PAD recognition while keeping targeted case-finding distinct from universal screening. METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through 31 July 2026, supplemented by citation searching and review of major US and European guidelines and relevant US policy and coverage sources. Evidence was interpreted according to the question it could answer: association/prognosis, diagnostic accuracy, treatment effect, implementation, or policy status. RESULTS: Hypertension and PAD share age-related, metabolic, renal, and tobacco-related determinants, while pressure-related vascular injury provides biological plausibility for their association. Resting ankle-brachial index (ABI) is the initial physiologic test for appropriately selected people; toe-brachial index with waveforms is preferred for noncompressible ankle arteries, exercise ABI for persistent exertional symptoms despite normal or borderline resting values, and duplex ultrasound when anatomic definition will change management. Guideline-supported risk-based testing differs from universal screening of unselected asymptomatic adults, for which outcome benefit remains unproven. Detection is clinically meaningful only when linked to appropriate prevention, symptom management, foot protection, and referral. CONCLUSION: This narrative review supports a risk-stratified, treatment-linked approach to PAD recognition in hypertension care, but the proposed case-finding pathway itself has not been proven to improve clinical outcomes. Pragmatic trials of the complete care pathway are needed.

title: An In Vitro Study Simulating Prophylactic Anticoagulation in Haemophilia A and B.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Patients with haemophilia A (HA) and haemophilia B (HB) are at increased bleeding risk. A recent guidance document suggests considering pharmacological thromboprophylaxis on a case-by-case basis in these patients undergoing surgery at high-risk of venous thromboembolism. This study aimed to assess the effect of prophylactic doses of three anticoagulants (enoxaparin, rivaroxaban and unfractionated heparin [UFH]) on in vitro models of HA and HB. METHODS: FVIII- and FIX-deficient plasma were spiked with FVIII and FIX concentrates to mimic severe, moderate and mild HA (FVIII concentrations < 1%, 1.2% and 17.0%, respectively) and HB (FIX concentrations < 1%, 3.9% and 22.9%, respectively). Each pool was spiked with enoxaparin (concentration range 0.3-0.4 IU/mL), rivaroxaban (50-100 ng/mL) and UFH (0.2-0.3 IU/mL). The following assays were performed: prothrombin time (PT), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) and thrombin generation (using the semi-automated fluorogenic calibrated automated thrombin generation assay [CAT]). RESULTS: The PT was not significantly affected by the anticoagulants. A significant prolongation of the APTT was observed; UFH showed the greatest increase, followed by rivaroxaban and enoxaparin. All anticoagulants impacted on the CAT curves. UFH showed the greatest reduction of the endogenous thrombin potential; rivaroxaban showed the greatest increase of lag time and time to peak. Peak thrombin and velocity index were similarly reduced by rivaroxaban and UFH, whereas enoxaparin was associated with smaller changes in all parameters. CONCLUSION: Trial Registration A significant effect of three prophylactic anticoagulants was observed in factor-deficient plasmas. This study provides further insight into this topic and supports the concept of an individualised approach to haemophilia patients.: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

title: In-Hospital Outcomes and Mortality After Revascularization for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia by Maintenance Dialysis Status: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2006-2020.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence on in-hospital outcomes after chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) revascularization in patients receiving maintenance dialysis is limited. METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression. RESULTS: Of 7,962 eligible hospitalizations, 411 (5.2% of the unweighted sample) involved maintenance dialysis. Maintenance dialysis was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.96), non-routine discharge (aOR 1.46), prolonged hospitalization (aOR 1.41), transfusion (aOR 1.43), sepsis (aOR 1.88), pneumonia (aOR 1.69), multiorgan failure or shock (aOR 1.80), and venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.06). Hospital charges were also higher (adjusted beta USD 17,497), whereas urinary tract infection odds were lower (aOR 0.68). DISCUSSION: Maintenance dialysis was associated with greater in-hospital morbidity and mortality among CMI-coded revascularization hospitalizations. The inability to distinguish stable from acute-on-chronic CMI limits interpretation as an elective cohort. Findings support individualized perioperative assessment without establishing causation or optimal treatment timing.

METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression.

title: Optimizing remote mechanical thrombectomy training using causal machine learning: a multicenter study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Remote, live-streamed mechanical thrombectomy (MT) training is a novel educational strategy, but its impact on patient outcomes remains unclear. The authors aimed to move beyond average treatment effects to identify which clinician subgroups derive the most significant clinical gains from cumulative training exposure. METHODS: In this prospective multicenter cohort study, 1010 clinicians participated in standardized, live-streamed MT training. The authors applied causal inference techniques, including double/debiased machine learning (DML), causal forest analysis, and Bayesian mixed-effects models, to evaluate the impact of cumulative training hours on 90-day patient outcomes. A Bayesian generalized linear mixed model was used to map personalized dose-response trajectories stratified by baseline clinical competency and surgical experience. RESULTS: Longer cumulative training hours was associated with improved procedural performance and better 90-day functional outcomes. DML models consistently showed significant treatment effects (0.83-0.85, p < 0.001). Bayesian mixed-effects modeling confirmed a strong association between training duration (OR 2.2, 95% CI 1.58-3.02) and clinician competency (score range 0-100; OR 3.7, 95% CI 2.79-4.86). Notably, while the training conferred universal clinical benefits across all baseline levels, the learning curve demonstrated continuous, linear improvements that were particularly pronounced among high-competency practitioners. CONCLUSIONS: Structured remote MT training was linked to improved procedural efficiency and functional recovery after stroke. These findings support the use of data-driven, personalized, and experience-stratified training strategies to enhance clinical practice and patient outcomes in stroke care.

title: Controversies and reappraisal in the management of distal deep vein thrombosis: From evidence-based discrepancies to risk-stratified individualized strategies.
abstract: BackgroundDistal deep vein thrombosis (DVT) confined to the infrapopliteal deep venous system, commonly termed isolated distal deep vein thrombosis (IDDVT), accounts for a substantial proportion of lower-extremity DVT. Its optimal management remains controversial because randomized evidence is limited, patient populations are heterogeneous, and guideline recommendations differ.ObjectiveThis narrative review critically examines the evidence for anticoagulation and serial ultrasonographic surveillance in IDDVT, evaluates sources of uncertainty, compares major guideline recommendations, and proposes a cautious, risk-adapted framework for individualized management.MethodsWe searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library to identify English-language guidelines, randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews/meta-analyses, and relevant observational studies addressing IDDVT management, thrombus extension, pulmonary embolism, bleeding, post-thrombotic syndrome, and treatment duration. The search was updated through July 2026. Priority was given to major guidelines, randomized trials, and contemporary systematic reviews/meta-analyses, with older studies retained when providing foundational evidence.ResultsCurrent evidence does not support a uniform treatment strategy for IDDVT. The choice between anticoagulation and serial imaging should consider symptom severity, extension risk factors, bleeding risk, thrombus location, patient preferences, and feasibility of follow-up imaging. Randomized trials support surveillance in selected patients and suggest reduced recurrent VTE with extended anticoagulation in patients who tolerate initial treatment. However, evidence remains limited by small or selected populations, heterogeneous outcomes, and extrapolation from proximal DVT or pulmonary embolism.ConclusionIDDVT should be managed according to individual risk rather than as a homogeneous condition. Decisions regarding anticoagulation initiation and treatment duration should be considered separately. Serial imaging is reasonable for selected patients without severe symptoms or major extension risk factors, whereas anticoagulation is generally favored in those with severe symptoms or recognized extension risk factors. No IDDVT-specific risk score has been validated, and interventional treatment should remain exceptional because direct evidence is lacking.

title: Deep inspiration-facilitated stenting for extremely tortuous vertebral artery ostium in a Type III arch.
abstract: Endovascular treatment of vertebral artery ostial (VAO) stenosis can be technically challenging in the presence of severe supra-aortic tortuosity, particularly a Type III aortic arch where stable guide catheter positioning is often difficult to maintain. During device delivery, inadequate proximal support may result in guide catheter prolapse into the aortic arch, compromising procedural success. Although adjunctive support techniques such as the buddy-wire technique may improve system stability, extreme vascular tortuosity can still impede the advancement of balloons or stents.1 A deep inspiration maneuver with transient breath-holding may facilitate device delivery by inducing caudal displacement of the aortic arch and proximal subclavian artery.2 Because the distal vertebral artery remains relatively fixed within the transverse foramina, this maneuver generates temporary axial tension across the V1 segment, partially straightening the tortuous vascular course and improving device trackability.3This technical video (video 1) demonstrates step-by-step endovascular reconstruction of an extremely tortuous right VAO lesion in a patient with prior failed stenting caused by hostile vascular anatomy and subsequent recurrent stenosis. Despite the Type III arch anatomy, a transfemoral approach was mandated over a radial approach due to the acute ostial geometry, providing the necessary antegrade delivery vector. We highlight a dual strategy approach combining distal wire-anchor support to enhance guiding stability and respiratory-induced vascular straightening to facilitate device navigation, ultimately enabling precise stent deployment and complete revascularization.neurintsurg;jnis-2026-025713v2/V1F1V1Video 1.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound for proximal lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis in emergency settings: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of emergency clinician-performed ultrasound for proximal lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and explore variation by scan protocol and operator group.MethodsThis systematic review and meta-analysis included studies of adults with suspected DVT in emergency settings. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to 8 April 2026, and a targeted literature update was conducted through 20 September 2026 during revision. A bivariate binomial random-effects model jointly estimated sensitivity and specificity. The primary analysis included one dataset per study to avoid duplicate weighting of paired cohorts. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed with QUADAS-2. Protocol and operator subgroup analyses were exploratory. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261361599).ResultsSixteen studies contributed quantitative data, providing 17 protocol datasets because one paired cohort was evaluated with both two-point and three-point protocols. Selecting the three-point result from that paired cohort for the primary overall model yielded 16 independent study datasets comprising 2,781 patient or limb/examination units. Pooled sensitivity was 0.91 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.85-0.95), and specificity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.91-0.97). Sensitivity estimates for two-point and three-point/extended protocols were 0.87 and 0.92, respectively. Source-data uncertainties, including a reconstructed diagnostic-analysis table in Jahanian 2019 and a provisional Crowhurst input, were examined in sensitivity analyses. Koylu 2026 was added during the revision-stage targeted literature update.ConclusionsEmergency clinician-performed ultrasound may support proximal DVT assessment within a defined diagnostic pathway. Negative limited examinations require interpretation alongside clinical probability and examination adequacy. Heterogeneity and unresolved source data limit confidence in the pooled estimates. Exploratory subgroup findings do not establish the superiority of any protocol or operator group.

title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference. DISCUSSION: + Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

title: High-intensity focused ultrasound as a bridging vascular-modulating therapy for fertility-sparing management of placental site trophoblastic tumor complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Placental site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT) is a rare gestational trophoblastic neoplasm characterized by local invasiveness and marked vascularity. Surgical management may be associated with substantial bleeding risk and loss of fertility, particularly when complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula (UAVF). High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) may provide a fertility-preserving adjunctive approach in selected cases. CASE PRESENTATION: A 23-year-old woman presented with persistently plateaued serum human chorionic gonadotropin levels following hysteroscopic management for suspected incomplete abortion. Imaging revealed a deeply invasive hypervascular uterine lesion with UAVF, raising strong suspicion of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Given her strong desire for fertility preservation and high surgical risk, ultrasound-guided HIFU was performed as an initial vascular-modulating intervention. Subsequent expert pathological review confirmed PSTT. RESULTS: HIFU achieved significant reduction in lesion perfusion and vascular flow, as confirmed by Doppler ultrasound and contrast-enhanced MRI. Although complete tumor ablation was not achieved due to lesion size and deep invasion, subsequent low-dose chemotherapy resulted in complete biochemical remission accompanied by radiologic regression of residual lesions. No major HIFU-related complications were observed, and normal menstrual function resumed during follow-up. CONCLUSION: HIFU is a technically feasible and safe fertility-preserving adjunct for vascular modulation in hypervascular PSTT complicated by UAVF. While HIFU alone may not achieve definitive oncologic control in large or deeply invasive lesions, it can serve as a bridging strategy to reduce tumor perfusion and vascularity, facilitating subsequent systemic therapy in carefully selected patients. This approach demonstrates the potential role of HIFU as a bridging vascular-modulating strategy within multimodal fertility-preserving management.

Surgical management may be associated with substantial bleeding risk and loss of fertility, particularly when complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula (UAVF). High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) may provide a fertility-preserving adjunctive approach in selected cases.

title: Association between neuromuscular electrical stimulation and intermittent pneumatic compression for the prevention of deep venous thrombosis among neurosurgery patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis. METHODS: Postoperative neurosurgical patients were retrospectively enrolled from a single centre between January 2020 and December 2021. These patients were assessed to have a high bleeding risk and received either NMES or IPC as mechanical prophylaxis. Univariable analysis was used to explore the risk factors for DVT, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent associations between DVT and potential variables after adjusting for confounding factors. RESULTS: p p p p Among 232 patients who underwent neurosurgery, 131 received IPC and 101 received NMES, with no overlap between the two groups. DVT was diagnosed in 62 patients (11 received NMES and 51 received IPC). After controlling for sex, age, operation duration and length of hospital stay, NMES use was associated with a lower incidence of DVT (OR = 0.268, 95% CI = 0.125-0.576, = .001). Moreover, men were less likely to have DVT than women (OR = 0.469, 95% CI = 0.242-0.910, = .025), older age was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 3.419, 95% CI = 1.594-7.334, = .002), and a longer operation duration was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 2.180, 95% CI = 1.042-4.560, = .039). CONCLUSION: This study found an association between NMES and reduced odds of DVT compared with IPC in neurosurgery patients. Although NMES may be more widely adopted in neurosurgery to decrease the incidence of DVT, further evidence is required to determine its effectiveness in clinical practice.

title: Prognostic Value of the Frailty Index in Patients with Severe Aortic Regurgitation Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty represents a multidimensional vulnerability that predicts poor outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the prospective China DVD2 multicenter cohort, 298 patients with isolated severe AR who underwent TAVR were included. Frailty was assessed preprocedurally using an abbreviated 8-9-item cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) encompassing functional, cognitive, nutritional, and clinical domains. The primary endpoint was one-year all-cause mortality. The cohort-derived FI threshold for mortality was derived using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP were applied. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed. RESULTS: The cohort-derived FI threshold was 0.407, classifying 32 patients as high frailty. High-FI patients exhibited greater symptom burden, higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, larger left atrial diameter, and elevated NT-proBNP. One-year mortality was significantly higher in the high-FI group compared with low-FI patients (15.6% vs 3.4%, P = 0.010). High FI was associated with higher one-year mortality in Model 3 (HR 4.00, 95% CI 1.18-13.50; P = 0.026). No significant multiplicative or additive interaction with NT-proBNP was observed. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing TAVR for severe native aortic regurgitation, a high FI was associated with higher one-year mortality. These findings extend prior evidence on the prognostic implications of frailty to this understudied population.

title: Imaging in tarsal tunnel syndrome: A case series.
abstract: Tarsal tunnel syndrome is an under-recognized yet potentially debilitating entrapment neuropathy that is often misdiagnosed due to its non-specific clinical presentation. This case series presents four representative cases of space-occupying lesions within the tarsal tunnel - ganglion cysts, varicose veins, lipomas, and peripheral nerve sheath tumors - with emphasis on high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging and complementary radiographic and ultrasound findings. We demonstrate the characteristic imaging hallmarks of these lesions, including their mass effect on the tibial neurovascular bundle, signal intensities, and enhancement patterns, to aid clinicians and radiologists in timely recognition of this condition.

title: A Branch-Specific Combined Fenestration Strategy for Chronic Aortic Dissection With Severe Paravisceral True Lumen Compression.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate a branch-specific combined fenestration strategy to address the technical challenges of severe true lumen (TL) compression during physician-modified fenestration (PMF)-based four-vessel visceral reconstruction in chronic aortic dissection (CAD). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled twenty-three consecutive patients with aneurysmal CAD and severe paravisceral TL compression (minimum functional TL diameter ≤10 mm) treated between January 2020 and December 2024. All patients underwent visceral reconstruction using anterior-branch PMF and bilateral renal in situ laser fenestration (ISLF) performed following TL expansion. Endpoints included technical success (complete four-vessel reconstruction), 30-day mortality, target-vessel patency, and TL expansion. RESULTS: Complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction was achieved in all 23 patients (92/92 target vessels). Renal ISLF was successful in all 46 renal arteries, with first-attempt success in 44 (96%). Distal aortic exclusion was required in 20 patients; one interval infrarenal rupture in the staged group was managed with emergency repair. Over a median follow-up of 17.0 months, primary target-vessel patency was 99% (91/92). The median minimum functional TL diameter increased from 8.0 mm preoperatively to 15.9 mm at one-year follow-up. No type I or III endoleak was identified. Thirty-day mortality was 0%. Transient spinal cord ischaemia occurred in one patient (4%), and acute kidney injury (KDIGO Stage 1) in two patients (9%), all resolving before discharge. CONCLUSION: In highly selected CAD patients with severe TL compression, this combined fenestration strategy enabled complete four-vessel visceral reconstruction with satisfactory early target-vessel patency and no target-vessel loss, though longer follow-up in larger cohorts is required.

All patients underwent visceral reconstruction using anterior-branch PMF and bilateral renal in situ laser fenestration (ISLF) performed following TL expansion.

title: Effect of a Nurse-Driven Early Mobilization Protocol on Biomarker Levels and Incidence of Deep Vein Thrombosis After Lower Extremity Fracture Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: To evaluate the effect of a nurse-driven early mobilization protocol on the incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), biomarker levels, and clinical outcomes in patients after lower extremity fracture surgery. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 205 patients who underwent surgery for traumatic unilateral lower extremity fractures (January 2023-June 2025). Patients were divided into a control group (conventional care, n=107) and an early mobilization group (nurse-driven protocol, n=98) using July 2024 as the implementation cutoff. Outcomes included postoperative DVT incidence, changes in D-dimer and C-reactive protein (CRP), bed rest duration, pain scores, length of stay, and complications. Repeated-measures ANOVA compared biomarker changes; binary logistic regression identified DVT risk factors. RESULTS: The early mobilization group had a significantly lower incidence of postoperative DVT than the control group (7.14% vs. 19.63%, P=0.009), with an absolute risk reduction of 12.49% and a relative risk reduction of 63.6%. Repeated-measures ANOVA showed significant between-group effects (F=22.33, P<0.001) and interaction effects (F=6.36, P<0.001) for CRP levels. After Bonferroni correction, the early mobilization group had significantly lower D-dimer and CRP levels at one week postoperatively and at discharge than the control group (P<0.0125). The early mobilization group also had significantly better outcomes in terms of bed rest duration (5.86±1.69 days vs. 6.38±1.54 days, P=0.021), NRS score on postoperative day 3 (3.27±1.15 vs. 4.54±1.47, P<0.001), and length of hospital stay (median 11.00 days vs. 13.00 days, P<0.001), as well as a lower complication rate (6.12% vs. 14.95%, P=0.041). Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified the early mobilization protocol (OR=0.27, 95%CI: 0.10-0.73, P=0.009), age (OR=1.05, 95%CI: 1.02-1.08, P=0.001), and postoperative day 1 D-dimer level (OR=1.25, 95%CI: 1.05-1.47, P=0.011) as independent factors influencing postoperative DVT. CONCLUSION: A nurse-driven early mobilization protocol effectively reduces the incidence of DVT after lower extremity fracture surgery, improves coagulation and inflammatory biomarker levels, shortens hospital stay, and does not increase complication risks. The protocol is safe and feasible and can be recommended as an adjunctive measure for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention after lower extremity fracture surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 205 patients who underwent surgery for traumatic unilateral lower extremity fractures (January 2023-June 2025). Patients were divided into a control group (conventional care, n=107) and an early mobilization group (nurse-driven protocol, n=98) using July 2024 as the implementation cutoff.

title: Comparative evaluation of carotid artery stent designs through a strict randomized evidence synthesis and assessment of local vascular responses.
abstract: Carotid artery stenting is an established endovascular option for carotid stenosis, but comparative clinical evidence for individual stent designs remains limited. Full-text reassessment confirmed five independent trials that randomized patients specifically to a stent device or stent-design strategy. Only two trials (204 patients; four standardized events) provided fully verified arm-level data for stroke, transient ischemic attack, or all-cause death within 30 days. The device evidence formed a sparse chain without a closed loop, and each direct comparison was informed by one trial. Bayesian network meta-analysis, treatment ranking, and node-splitting were therefore not performed. Direct estimates were imprecise and did not establish superiority of any stent or structural class. The animal findings describe exploratory local vascular responses to geometry-matched miniature nitinol stents under controlled experimental conditions and do not validate a clinical device hierarchy. The chronological relationship between the clinical evidence review and animal study design is acknowledged as a limitation.

title: Clinical outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair by in situ microneedle fenestration using the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique.
abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the outcomes of total endovascular aortic arch repair (TEAAR) via in situ micro-needle fenestration (ISMNF) with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, the data of consecutive patients who underwent TEAAR via ISMNF with triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique between August 2022 and April 2025 were analyzed. Three 6-Fr, 90-cm sheaths were placed into ascending aorta without removing the dilator and super-stiff guidewires during main stent-graft deployment. This configuration creates a gutter between the stent-graft and aortic wall to maintain perfusion to supra-aortic branches. Operative details, technical success, 30-day and midterm outcomes, and adverse events were recorded. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate freedom from all-cause death and reintervention. RESULTS: Overall, 36 patients were included. The technical success rate was 94.4% (34/36). Endovascular reconstruction of cervical branches was successfully performed in all cases. The 30-day mortality was 2.8%. The median follow-up period was 19 months (range, 1-32 months). The all-cause death rate was 11.1% (4/36), with no cases of any aorta-related death. The prevalence of endoleaks during follow-up was 13.9% (5/36). The overall stroke rate was 8.3% (3/36). The 1- and 2-year survival rates were 97.3% ± 2.7% and 85.8% ± 8.1%, respectively. The cumulative rate of freedom from reintervention at 1 and 2 years was 87.5% ± 5.9% and 83.2% ± 7.0%, respectively. CONCLUSION: TEAAR via ISMNF with the triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique was performed with a 94% technical success rate and stroke risk similar to open surgery.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, the data of consecutive patients who underwent TEAAR via ISMNF with triple (stiff)-sheathed gutter technique between August 2022 and April 2025 were analyzed. Three 6-Fr, 90-cm sheaths were placed into ascending aorta without removing the dilator and super-stiff guidewires during main stent-graft deployment.

title: Characteristics of treatment responses to physical exercise and diet in diabetic peripheral artery disease patients: a systematic review.
abstract: PURPOSE: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects walking performance and increases risk of amputation. Diabetes mellitus (DM) not only contributes to disease progression but may also affect treatment effects. Though physical exercise is crucial in PAD management and diet optimization may reduce risk of atherosclerosis, their effects and variations in diabetic PAD patients remain unclear. The present systematic review aims to summarize features of treatment response to physical exercise and diet management in diabetic PAD patients, and provide crucial information on optimization of PAD management of these patients in clinical practice. METHODS: A systematic review was performed on human studies investigating effects of physical exercise and diet on development and improvement of diabetic PAD patients by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL. The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analysis (PRISMA). The certainty level of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). RESULTS: A total of 18 studies were included, 15 of which evaluated effects of exercise on diabetic PAD, and three evaluated correlation between diet and diabetic PAD. Supervised exercise therapy (SET) and home-based exercise were able to improve ankle-brachial index (ABI) and blood flow velocity in diabetic PAD. In contrast, walking performance such as the six minute walk distance (6MWD), maximal walking time and distance, peak walking time (PWT) and claudication onset time (COT) were not significantly improved or presented conflicting results. Administration of multiple exercises or alternative interventions such as shock wave therapy or low-frequency pulsed electromagnetic field therapy (LFPMT) may enhance improvement of ABI. Adherence to Mediterranean diet was associated with blood flow and intermittent claudication, as well as risk of development of PAD. GRADE analysis revealed very low to moderate grade evidence for findings on ABI, flow velocity and functions, mainly due to study types, number of studies available, small sample size, moderate risk of bias and conflicting results. Similarly, low grade evidence was also revealed for effects and association of diet on risk of PAD due to study type and number of studies available. CONCLUSION: Diabetic PAD patients may present reduced treatment response to physical exercise in walking performance and other functions, which may be improved by combination of multiple physical exercises or alternative interventions with or without combination of exercise. Mediterranean diet may be associated with beneficial effects, which requires further investigations. These findings were of very low to moderate level of certainty, and therefore, further validation is warranted in the future.

Diabetes mellitus (DM) not only contributes to disease progression but may also affect treatment effects. Though physical exercise is crucial in PAD management and diet optimization may reduce risk of atherosclerosis, their effects and variations in diabetic PAD patients remain unclear.

title: Dissecting cell-type-specific genetic associations between colorectal cancer liability and thrombotic risk in peripheral blood immune cells.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether CRC-associated thrombotic susceptibility includes cell-specific inherited regulatory components in peripheral blood remains unclear. To investigate associations between CRC genetic liability and VTE-related outcomes within peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) regulatory contexts. We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR). Prioritized signals were further examined in single-cell RNA-seq datasets and bulk transcriptomes. Conventional MR showed no clear evidence that CRC liability increased VTE, DVT, or PE risk, and LD Score regression detected no significant genome-wide genetic correlation. In contrast, csMR identified nominal, cell-context-dependent associations. B intermediate cells were prioritized across VTE (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32), DVT (OR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.08-1.57), and PE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.07-1.49), while CD14 + monocytes and CD4 + central memory T cells received additional support from downstream single-cell analyses. Gene-level analyses prioritized LAMA5, LIMA1, and TRIM28 in these respective cell contexts. In bulk blood, RPS21 showed consistent disease-associated expression patterns and discriminated VTE patients from healthy controls in an external dataset (AUC, 0.865; 95% CI, 0.800-0.923). These findings suggest that genetic overlap between CRC liability and thrombotic phenotypes may be localized to selected PBMC regulatory contexts rather than broadly detectable genome-wide. Among the prioritized signals, B intermediate cells showed the most consistent csMR associations across VTE, DVT, and PE. The cell-gene pairs, together with RPS21, warrant independent genetic, functional, and prospective validation as candidates for studying peripheral immune regulation and blood-based markers of CRC-associated thrombosis.

We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR).

title: Association of modified cardiovascular health with long-term all-cause mortality among adults with Ankle-Brachial Index-defined peripheral artery disease: a NHANES 1999-2004 cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether an integrated cardiovascular health profile is associated with long-term mortality among adults with objectively defined peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains insufficiently characterized in nationally representative cohorts. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥40 years with Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) measurements and linked mortality follow-up through December 31, 2019. PAD was defined as a minimum ABI ≤0.90. Modified cardiovascular health (mCVH; range 0-12) was constructed from smoking, Body Mass Index, physical activity, blood pressure, total cholesterol, and glycemic status. Corrected six-year Mobile Examination Center weights and complex survey design variables were used. Weighted Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for all-cause mortality using sequential adjustment for demographic factors, socioeconomic factors, survey cycle, and minimum ABI. Additional analyses evaluated non-PAD participants and cardiovascular mortality. RESULTS: The primary PAD cohort included 554 adults, among whom 428 deaths occurred during a median follow-up of 123.5 months. PAD participants had a higher absolute all-cause mortality burden than non-PAD participants. Each 1-point higher mCVH score was associated with lower all-cause mortality in Model 1 (HR 0.888, 95% CI 0.842-0.937; P<0.001), Model 2 (HR 0.922, 95% CI 0.870-0.977; P=0.006), and Model 3 (HR 0.926, 95% CI 0.874-0.982; P=0.010). Among non-PAD participants, higher mCVH was also associated with lower all-cause mortality, and the mCVH × PAD status interaction was not statistically significant (P=0.122). In sensitivity analysis, higher mCVH was also associated with lower cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.863, 95% CI 0.786-0.948; P=0.002). Component-level analyses suggested that smoking was the most robust individual component. CONCLUSIONS: Among U.S. adults with ABI-defined PAD, higher baseline mCVH was associated with lower long-term all-cause mortality. These findings support the prognostic relevance of integrated cardiovascular health profiling after objective PAD identification, while highlighting smoking as the most consistent individual component.

METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥40 years with Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) measurements and linked mortality follow-up through December 31, 2019. PAD was defined as a minimum ABI ≤0.90.
