title: Outcomes of hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation (HEPATIC): an international, multicentre, retrospective registry study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is a severe complication that can lead to acute graft failure, often requiring urgent re-transplantation. We aimed to assess the 1-year incidence of graft loss and mortality and to evaluate outcomes according to the timing of hepatic artery thrombosis and the treatment approaches in patients with hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation. METHODS: In this international, multicentre, retrospective study, the HEPATIC registry, which had 33 centres across 21 countries as of December, 2025, was used to identify patients who developed hepatic artery thrombosis at age younger than 18 years after paediatric liver transplantation between Jan 1, 2002, and Dec 31, 2021, and who either received a diagnosis of or received an intervention for hepatic artery thrombosis before Jan 1, 2023. Donor-related, recipient-related, and transplantation-related characteristics collected from local medical records were entered retrospectively into electronic case reports by participating centres, with centralised data quality control. Primary outcomes were 1-year graft loss and mortality after hepatic artery thrombosis diagnosis. The outcomes were examined based on when hepatic artery thrombosis occurred after paediatric liver transplantation (early [≤7 days] vs late [>7 days]), primary management strategy (conservative management, surgical revascularisation, endovascular therapy, or immediate listing for re-transplantation), and transplantation era (in 5-year intervals). The registry was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05818644. FINDINGS: Hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 415 patients, of whom 216 (52%) were female and 199 (48%) were male, and median age was 1·7 years (IQR 0·8-6·5). Median follow-up was 50·9 months (IQR 17·0-112·6). Graft loss occurred in 180 patients by 1 month (cumulative incidence 43% [95% CI 38-48]) and 222 by 1 year (54% [49-58]); 51 patients died by 1 month (12% [9-15]) and 77 by 1 year (19% [15-22]). Surgical revascularisation was the first-line treatment approach in 195 (47%) patients. Other strategies included listing for re-transplantation in 99 (24%), conservative management in 79 (19%), and endovascular therapy in 42 (10%). Treatment approaches changed over time, with increased use of conservative management and endovascular therapy and reduced listing for re-transplantation (p<0·0001), with no accompanying change in 1-year mortality across eras (p=0·14). Early (≤7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 282 (68%) patients and was associated with higher 1-year graft loss than late (>7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis (cumulative incidence 57% [95% CI 51-63] vs 47% [37-55], log-rank p=0·010). Surgical revascularisation was used in 167 (59%) patients and listing for re-transplantation in 66 (23%) patients with early hepatic artery thrombosis, whereas conservative management was used in 51 (38%) patients and endovascular therapy in 21 (16%) patients with late hepatic artery thrombosis; however, 1-year mortality did not differ between treatment strategies among patients with early versus late hepatic artery thrombosis. INTERPRETATION: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is associated with notably high 1-year graft loss and mortality, particularly if hepatic artery thrombosis occurs within 7 days after the procedure. The management strategies for hepatic artery thrombosis differ according to the post-transplantation timing of hepatic artery thrombosis occurrence. Despite changes in management over the past 20 years, outcomes have remained poor, underscoring the need to improve therapeutic strategies for this complication. FUNDING: None.

title: Anatomical distribution of lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism: a retrospective study with finite-element analysis of calf muscle-vein mechanics.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Muscular calf vein thrombosis is frequently detected by whole-leg ultrasonography, but its relationship with pulmonary embolism (PE) and the mechanical response of the intramuscular veins during calf-muscle contraction remain incompletely defined. We examined PE prevalence across anatomical categories of lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and used a structural finite-element model to quantify contraction-related venous compression and identify the regions in which deformation was greatest. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients evaluated for a first episode of lower-extremity DVT between May and October 2022. DVT was classified as isolated muscular calf vein thrombosis, isolated axial calf DVT, isolated proximal DVT, or combined muscular calf and proximal DVT. PE was diagnosed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography or pulmonary perfusion imaging. Because several cells contained few observations, the four-group distribution was compared using a Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test. A separate finite-element analysis used one normal computed tomography angiography geometry. Gastrocnemius contraction, soleus contraction, and co-contraction were modeled as structural loading conditions. Spatial stress and strain maps were examined to localize venous regions with the greatest structural response. No blood-flow, venous-valve, or thrombus model was included. RESULTS: p 3 Among 160 patients with DVT, 30 had PE. PE was present in 14 of 125 patients with isolated muscular calf vein thrombosis [11.2%, exact 95% confidence interval (CI): 6.3%-18.1%], 1 of 4 with isolated axial calf DVT (25.0%, 95% CI: 0.6%-80.6%), 3 of 10 with isolated proximal DVT (30.0%, 95% CI: 6.7%-65.2%), and 12 of 21 with combined muscular calf and proximal DVT (57.1%, 95% CI: 34.0%-78.2%). The overall distribution differed across groups (exact < 0.001). At the final recorded model-loading parameter, mean muscle von Mises stress was 21.51 kPa during gastrocnemius contraction, 1.16 kPa during soleus contraction, and 9.68 kPa during co-contraction. The corresponding changes in modeled venous-domain volume were -49.25, -17.07, and -64.08 mm, respectively. The spatial maps showed nonuniform venous deformation, with the most prominent response concentrated around proximal branching regions and adjacent intramuscular venous segments. CONCLUSIONS: PE prevalence differed across the anatomical DVT categories and was highest when muscular calf and proximal veins were involved concurrently. The structural model provided direct evidence that calf-muscle contraction compresses deep veins and localized the regions of greatest deformation. These findings support targeted dynamic venous imaging, while effects on blood flow and thrombus behavior require prospective patient-specific validation.

METHODS: This retrospective study included patients evaluated for a first episode of lower-extremity DVT between May and October 2022.

title: Association of red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Critically ill patients with aortic dissection remain at high risk of adverse ICU outcomes, including ICU mortality. The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been investigated as a prognostic marker in various clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the association of RAR with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection. METHODS: Data were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. ICU mortality was defined as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay, acute kidney injury (AKI), and renal replacement therapy (RRT) use. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess the discriminative performance of RAR for ICU mortality. The optimal RAR cutoff was determined using Youden's index and was considered exploratory. Calibration plots and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance. RESULTS: P P P RAR showed modest discrimination for ICU mortality (AUC: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.552-0.765). The exploratory cutoff value of RAR was 5.182. Compared with the low-RAR group, the high-RAR group had higher ICU mortality (21.8% vs. 6.7%; < 0.001), a higher prevalence of sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay (82.8% vs. 61.1%; < 0.001), and more frequent RRT use (33.3% vs. 9.4%; < 0.001). The AUC increased from 0.706 for SOFA alone to 0.731 for SOFA plus RAR, indicating only limited incremental discrimination. CONCLUSION: Higher early-ICU RAR was associated with ICU mortality and other adverse ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection, but its discrimination was modest, its incremental value beyond SOFA was limited, and external validation is required.

The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been investigated as a prognostic marker in various clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the association of RAR with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection.

title: From recanalization to recovery: inflammation and futile reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has markedly improved reperfusion outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion. However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion. This clinical-angiographic mismatch may reflect persistent tissue injury, including inflammatory injury, alongside pretreatment damage and other determinants of outcome. Experimental findings and clinical associations implicate persistent inflammatory activation, thrombo-inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, microvascular no-reflow, and blood-brain barrier disruption as contributors to secondary tissue injury after MT. Here, we examine potential inflammatory contributions to futile reperfusion and consider how inflammatory biomarkers might inform risk stratification after MT. Ischemia activates microglia, endothelial cells, platelets, complement pathways, and circulating immune cells. Subsequent reperfusion may amplify oxidative stress, cytokine signaling, neutrophil-endothelial interactions, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, matrix metalloproteinase activity, and barrier failure. Together, these processes can promote microvascular obstruction, cerebral edema, hemorrhagic transformation, infarct growth, and impaired neurological recovery despite successful angiographic reperfusion. Among circulating biomarkers, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio has been studied repeatedly, alongside platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, interleukin-6, matrix metalloproteinase-9, and other molecular markers. Their specificity, incremental predictive value, and clinical utility require further validation in standardized thrombectomy cohorts. We therefore view inflammation as a plausible biological link between macrovascular reperfusion and persistent tissue-level injury after MT. From a translational perspective, the immediate priorities are to standardize sampling protocols, characterize dynamic inflammatory trajectories, develop multimodal prediction models, and test biomarker-guided therapeutic strategies.

However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding venous thromboembolism prevention in patients with lung cancer.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with lung cancer are at high risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet their awareness and preventive behaviors remain insufficiently characterized. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding VTE prevention among patients with lung cancer and explored factors associated with these dimensions. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 244 patients with lung cancer recruited at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital between January and May 2026. Participants completed a KAP questionnaire regarding VTE prevention. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with KAP outcomes, and Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine the associations among knowledge, attitudes, and practices. RESULTS: The mean knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were 8.98 ± 3.52, 31.18 ± 3.37, and 19.19 ± 4.49, respectively. Rural or suburban residence (adjusted OR = 0.447, 95% CI 0.201-0.992) and no previous VTE education (adjusted OR = 0.271, 95% CI 0.147-0.501) were associated with lower odds of meeting the operational knowledge threshold. Higher knowledge scores were associated with more favorable attitudes and higher self-reported preventive practice scores, while higher attitude scores were associated with higher self-reported preventive practice scores. CONCLUSION: Patients with lung cancer showed persistent gaps in VTE-related knowledge, generally favorable responses to several attitude items, and heterogeneous self-reported preventive behaviors. The findings highlight potential targets for patient education, particularly among rural or suburban residents and those without previous VTE education.

This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding VTE prevention among patients with lung cancer and explored factors associated with these dimensions. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 244 patients with lung cancer recruited at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital between January and May 2026.

title: Machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with venous thromboembolism and acute kidney injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI. METHODS: n n In this retrospective study, data from 585 ICU patients with VTE and AKI were analyzed. Patients were divided into a training cohort ( = 409) and a validation cohort ( = 176). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with standardization was applied for feature selection. Five machine learning models-logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM)-were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis (DCA), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and feature importance were performed for the optimal model. The performance of the best machine learning model was compared with conventional ICU severity scores (APSIII, LODs, and OASIS). RESULTS: The standardized LASSO regression identified ten optimal predictors: creatinine (cr), age, tumor/cancer, body mass index (BMI), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), urine output, D-dimer (D_D), Charlson comorbidity index, anticoagulant use, and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). Among the five models, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance with a validation AUC of 0.882 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.832-0.924], followed by RF (AUC = 0.878), LightGBM (AUC = 0.870), LR (AUC = 0.838), and SVM (AUC = 0.662). The 5-fold cross-validation AUC for XGBoost was 0.901 ± 0.042, with minimal overfitting (CV-test difference = -0.019). Decision curve analysis demonstrated favorable clinical net benefit of the XGBoost model across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis and feature importance consistently identified urine output, age, LDL, BMI, and D-dimer as the top contributors. Compared with conventional ICU severity scores, the XGBoost model significantly outperformed APSIII (AUC = 0.661), LODs (AUC = 0.652), and OASIS (AUC = 0.647). The logistic regression-based nomogram achieved a C-index of 0.838, providing a user-friendly bedside tool for clinicians. CONCLUSION: The machine learning-based XGBoost model, incorporating ten readily available clinical variables, demonstrated excellent predictive performance for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with VTE and AKI. This model offers a practical and interpretable tool for early risk stratification and may guide proactive nutritional and therapeutic interventions in this vulnerable population.

This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI.

title: Factors associated with mortality in patients with atrial fibrillation: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study synthesized published meta-analyses to assess the quality, bias, and strength of evidence regarding mortality risk factors in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). METHODS: Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane database were used to search the literature up to May 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews or meta-analyses investigating AF-related mortality risk factors. AMSTAR tool was used to assess methodological quality and GRADE was used to evaluate evidence certainty. RESULTS: A total of 216 risk factors were identified. Among them, 86 showed significant associations with mortality, while 130 did not. Based on GRADE ratings, 11 were high-quality significant factors, and 9 were of moderate-quality. Factors linked to increased mortality included certain medications (digoxin, dronedarone, sotalol; warfarin/VKA vs. NOAC was associated with higher mortality), comorbidities (cancer, COPD, diabetes, anemia, frailty, LVH, peripheral artery disease), demographic characteristics (older age, smoking, BMI <18.5, Latin American ethnicity), and AF subtype (persistent or non-paroxysmal). In contrast, reduced mortality was associated with NOAC or DOAC use, higher BMI (25-30 or ≥30), surgical interventions (catheter ablation, LAAC/LAAO), other medications (SGLT2 inhibitors, statins), and early rhythm control. CONCLUSION: Systematic Review Registration: This review highlights key factors associated with mortality in AF. Increased risk was observed with warfarin/VKA use (vs. NOAC), certain antiarrhythmic drugs, comorbidities, low BMI, older age, smoking, and non-paroxysmal AF. In contrast, NOAC use, surgical interventions, high BMI, statin and SGLT2 inhibitor therapy, and early rhythm-control strategies were linked to reduced mortality risk.https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024533372, PROSPERO CRD42024533372.

title: Deep Learning-Based Versus Threshold-Based Bone Removal for CT Angiography of Head and Neck Arteriovenous Fistulas: A Retrospective Comparison of Image Quality, Key-Structure Display, and Post-Processing Time.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p Bone overlap at the skull base limits CT angiography (CTA) in head and neck arteriovenous fistulas (hAVFs), and threshold-based bone removal fails where bone and contrast attenuation overlap. Whether deep learning-based removal improves the display of the structures that determine endovascular planning is unknown in a DSA-confirmed cohort. We therefore compared the two methods within the same CTA datasets.In this single-centre retrospective study, 35 patients with DSA-confirmed hAVF underwent head and neck CTA and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) within two weeks of each other, and each CTA dataset was post-processed with both methods on one workstation. Two blinded readers scored the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein (0 to 2 each) and overall image quality (5-point scale). Scores were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, vessel edge sharpness and post-processing time with paired t tests, and technical visualisation with McNemar's test.Deep learning-based removal displayed the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein more completely (median total anatomical score 6.00 versus 3.00;< 0.001 for both readers) and overall image quality was higher (5.00 versus 4.00;< 0.001). Objective vessel edge sharpness was concordant (316.47 ± 46.68 versus 273.70 ± 45.66 HU/mm;< 0.001). Technical visualisation was numerically higher (97.1% versus 88.6%) but not significantly so (= 0.248; three discordant pairs), which makes this endpoint inconclusive rather than negative. Post-processing time was shorter (40.56 ± 1.61 s versus 101.70 ± 4.39 s; mean paired difference 61.14 s, 95% CI 59.53 to 62.74 s; paired t test,< 0.001).In DSA-confirmed hAVF, deep learning-based bone removal displayed the structures that determine endovascular planning more completely than threshold-based removal and was about one minute faster per case. It does not replace DSA for definitive assessment of fistula architecture, and the apparent advantage at the cavernous sinus is exploratory and requires external validation in larger multicentre cohorts.

title: Development and internal validation of a clinical prediction model for postoperative venous thromboembolism after neurosurgical intervention in patients with traumatic brain injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a critical complication after traumatic brain injury (TBI) surgery. Conventional risk assessment tools were not developed for neurosurgical trauma populations, limiting their applicability. OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally validate an interpretable clinical prediction model for postoperative VTE in TBI surgery patients. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 1,450 TBI patients who underwent surgery (2016-2024). Seven predictors were selected using Recursive Feature Elimination. Six machine learning algorithms were compared, with logistic regression (LR) selected as the final model. Performance was evaluated using AUC-ROC, calibration, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Among 1,450 patients, 205 (14.1%) developed postoperative VTE. The LR model achieved AUC-ROC of 0.868 (95% CI: 0.815-0.920) with good calibration (Brier score: 0.085). Seven predictors were identified: age, Barthel index, ASA classification, multiple surgeries, general anesthesia, limb AIS score, and serum magnesium. Compared with Caprini score (AUC: 0.686), the model showed improved discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.182; NRI: 0.559). CONCLUSION: An interpretable model based on seven routinely available variables demonstrated promising performance for postoperative VTE risk stratification in TBI surgery patients. A nomogram and web-based calculator are provided for clinical use.

Conventional risk assessment tools were not developed for neurosurgical trauma populations, limiting their applicability. title: A clinical-deep learning model for prolonged length of stay following endovascular aortic repair.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prolonged length of stay (PLOS) after endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is associated with increased complications, resource burden, and patient distress. Early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating clinical variables and three-dimensional deep learning (3D-DL) features from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) to predict PLOS after EVAR. METHODS: A total of 788 patients with AAA who underwent elective EVAR were enrolled from two hospitals. The internal training cohort consisted of 556 patients, and the external validation cohort included 232 patients. PLOS was defined as a LOS above the 75th percentile of the distribution. A clinical nomogram was developed using LASSO regression followed by multivariate logistic regression. Deep learning (DL) features were extracted from manually segmented computed tomography angiography (CTA) images using a 3D ResNet200 network, and LASSO regression was applied to select the most informative features. An ensemble model integrating the clinical predictors and the selected DL features was constructed. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: LASSO combined with multivariate logistic regression identified five independent clinical predictors: age, hemoglobin, albumin, maximum aneurysm diameter, and diabetes. The clinical model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.917 in the internal cohort and 0.944 in the external cohort. From the 3D ResNet200 network, 32 DL features were extracted. LASSO regression further selected two of these features. The ensemble predictive model, which integrated the clinical predictors and DL features, demonstrated improved discrimination, with an AUC of 0.971 in the internal cohort and 0.958 in the external cohort. Internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples yielded optimism-corrected AUCs of 0.911 for the clinical model and 0.966 for the ensemble model. Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent model performance across age and diabetes strata, while performance in the female subgroup warrants further evaluation in larger cohorts. CONCLUSION: This study developed an ensemble predictive model to predict PLOS following EVAR. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination and provided significant prognostic value beyond clinical variables alone. This nomogram may serve as a preoperative tool for risk stratification and resource planning in this population. Future studies should focus on prospective validation and clinical integration.

Early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating clinical variables and three-dimensional deep learning (3D-DL) features from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) to predict PLOS after EVAR.

title: Case Report: Endovascular repair for true lumen collapse after frozen elephant trunk for type A aortic dissection.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Frozen elephant trunk (FET) was applied in the treatment of type A aortic dissection, enabling one-stage repair of the aortic arch and proximal descending aorta while promoting true lumen expansion. However, inadvertent FET deployment into the false lumen is a rare but catastrophic complication that may cause true lumen collapse and life-threatening visceral malperfusion, with limited reports on its endovascular management. CASE PRESENTATION: Here, we present the case of a 44-year-old female who underwent Bentall procedure, total arch replacement, and FET implantation for acute type A aortic dissection at a local hospital. Postoperatively, she developed visceral malperfusion manifesting as abdominal distension, hepatic and renal dysfunction, and elevated lactate levels. Computed tomography angiography revealed that the FET stent had been inadvertently deployed into the false lumen, resulting in true lumen collapse. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed, establishing a "FET-false lumen-true lumen" pathway with an additional stent graft to redirect aortic flow into the true lumen. Computational fluid dynamics analysis showed that the postoperative hemodynamics have been significantly improved. The patient's organ function normalized, and she was discharged two weeks later, remaining asymptomatic at 8-month follow-up. CONCLUSION: Endovascular reintervention with additional stent grafting to establish a flow-redirection pathway is a feasible and effective strategy for true lumen collapse following inadvertent FET deployment into the false lumen. Prompt recognition, timely imaging confirmation, and immediate intervention are paramount to mitigating the risks associated with this serious complication.

title: Advances in Design and Preparation of Biodegradable Inferior Vena Cava Filters.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with pulmonary embolism (PE) constituting its most fatal clinical consequence. Inferior vena cava filters (IVCFs) have been employed as a mechanical prophylactic strategy for patients with contraindications to anticoagulation or recurrent embolic events. However, permanent implantation and limited retrieval success are associated with device-related complications, including caval perforation, migration, fracture, and filter-induced thrombosis. Biodegradable IVCFs have been investigated as an alternative approach to provide temporary protection while avoiding the complications associated with long-term implantation. This review discusses recent advances in biodegradable IVCFs from a material perspective, focusing on material selection, structural design, degradation characteristics, and biological responses. Biodegradable polymers, degradable metallic materials, and shape-memory systems are evaluated regarding their mechanical stability, degradation behavior, vascular compatibility, and functional requirements. Strategies for improving radiopacity while preserving biodegradability are also summarized. Despite ongoing progress, key challenges remain in precisely controlling degradation kinetics, maintaining adequate mechanical support during the therapeutic period, and validating long-term safety through clinical studies. Further efforts in material optimization, biofunctional modification, and individualized fabrication may facilitate the future development of biodegradable IVCFs.

title: Redox Dysregulation in the Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Wall: Ferroptosis and Experimental Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a spatially heterogeneous disease of the aortic wall for which no pharmacological treatment has reliably arrested enlargement. The term oxidative stress encompasses processes that differ in chemical form, anatomical location and cellular effect. This narrative review examines haem and redox-active iron, phospholipid peroxidation and antioxidant defence at the intraluminal thrombus-wall interface and within medial and inflammatory cells. We distinguish ferroptosis from redox effects on coagulation, migration and secretion and relate these functions to wall remodelling. Experimental studies show that manipulating iron uptake and ferritin turnover, membrane phospholipid susceptibility or peroxide detoxification can alter vascular smooth muscle cell survival, macrophage behaviour and aortic injury. The cellular function affected helps determine which process an intervention should preserve or suppress. Based on evidence from human tissue and animal models, we review opportunities to localise, manipulate and monitor these processes and assess their relevance to established AAA. Testing after confirmation of aneurysm formation, with target engagement in defined wall cells and parallel assessment of systemic effects, is needed to determine whether these approaches can limit continued enlargement.

title: The Central Coupler of ClpXP Controls Intersubunit Communication and Couples Intrasubunit Chemical Energy with Force Generation.
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

title: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in bicuspid versus tricuspid aortic valves among patients with mixed aortic valve disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mixed aortic valve disease (MAVD), defined as the coexistence of significant aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation (AR), presents unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Prior studies rarely distinguished bicuspid valve morphology in MAVD populations, and no study has evaluated long-term transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) outcomes between bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) patients in this setting. The aim is to investigate the clinical outcomes of BAV versus TAV morphology in patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR. METHODS: Between March 2013 and December 2024, 610 MAVD patients undergoing TAVR were included. Patients with severe AS and concomitant presence of moderate or more severe aortic regurgitation were defined as the MAVD. Clinical outcomes, functional status and echocardiography were followed and compared. RESULTS: A total of 610 patients were included in this study, 220 (36.1%) of whom were BAV morphology. BAV patients were younger (73 vs. 75 years, p < 0.001) and had a lower Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score (3.47% vs. 4.15%, p < 0.001) compared to TAV patients. The five-year mortality rate was lower in bicuspid than tricuspid patients (10.5% vs. 18.7%, log-rank p = 0.014), while Cox regression analysis did not indicate BAV as an independent predictor of five-year all-cause mortality after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] 0.75, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.47-1.22, p = 0.253). During the one-year follow-up after procedure, BAV patients exhibited a greater increase in AVA and LVEF (p for interaction = 0.012 and 0.011, respectively), and a greater reduction in mean gradient and peak velocity (both p for interaction < 0.001). Meanwhile, similar left ventricular reverse remodelling was found during follow-up (both p for trend < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In MAVD patients undergoing TAVR, bicuspid and tricuspid valve morphologies demonstrated comparable long-term clinical outcomes. BAV patients demonstrated greater improvements in left ventricular function and transvalvular hemodynamics, suggesting that bicuspid morphology itself does not confer an adverse long-term prognostic effect in appropriately selected patients with MAVD undergoing TAVR. title: Spatial Signatures of Retinal Neurodegeneration in Glaucoma, Alzheimer's Disease, and Carotid Stenosis.
abstract: PURPOSE: To compare spatial and topographical signatures of inner retinal alterations across primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG), Alzheimer's disease (AD), and carotid artery stenosis (CAS). METHODS: This multicenter cross-sectional study included 1380 participants: 695 healthy controls (HCs), 331 with POAG, 105 with AD, and 249 with CAS. Peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (pRNFL) and macular ganglion cell layer (GCL) thicknesses were measured using optical coherence tomography (OCT). Spatial dispersion metrics, including vertical asymmetry, maximum-minimum (Max-Min) difference, and coefficient of variation, were derived to characterize intraeye spatial heterogeneity. RESULTS: POAG showed profound global pRNFL and GCL thinning, whereas AD and CAS had preserved global pRNFL thickness. Spatial analysis revealed distinct anatomic patterns. POAG was characterized by marked compression of the pRNFL sectoral thickness range (reduced Max-Min difference; P < 0.001). In contrast, AD and CAS maintained or increased pRNFL spatial variability. AD showed selective temporal pRNFL thinning (P = 0.002) without significant macular GCL thinning, whereas CAS showed generalized macular GCL thinning with temporal pRNFL vulnerability (both P < 0.05). The pRNFL Max-Min difference showed high apparent discrimination for differentiating POAG from HC, AD, and CAS, outperforming conventional global thickness metrics, but requires external validation. CONCLUSIONS: Retinal neurodegeneration exhibits etiology-specific spatial architectures. Intraeye spatial heterogeneity metrics may help distinguish glaucomatous optic neuropathy from central neurodegenerative and chronic ischemic conditions, although validation in independent and early-stage cohorts is needed. TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE: Spatial OCT metrics may aid differentiation of glaucomatous and nonglaucomatous retinal neurodegeneration.

Peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (pRNFL) and macular ganglion cell layer (GCL) thicknesses were measured using optical coherence tomography (OCT).

title: Failure Modes of Endovascular Therapy for Spontaneous Isolated Superior Mesenteric Artery Dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mechanisms of failure after endovascular stenting for symptomatic spontaneous isolated superior mesenteric artery dissection (SISMAD) remain poorly characterized. We analyzed device- and procedure-related failure modes in a 17-year single-center cohort. METHODS: We reviewed 117 consecutive patients with SISMAD (2008-2025). Patients stented for persistent or escalating pain despite conservative management formed the cohort; catheter-infusion and open-surgery patients were analyzed separately. Lesions were classified by Yun morphology. Failure modes were classified a priori as type I (intraprocedural technical failure), type II (thrombotic events occurring after the procedure), and type III (in-stent restenosis or intimal hyperplasia at ≥6 months). Patency and reinterventions were recorded. RESULTS: Thirty-two patients underwent endovascular therapy (28 stenting, 4 catheter-directed infusion). In the stent cohort, uncomplicated technical success was 82.1% (23/28). Type I failures occurred in 17.9% (5/28), dominated by false-lumen deployment (10.7%) clustered in Yun III occlusions (50.0% vs. 9.1%; P = 0.050). Type II events (3 weeks; 24 months) were rescued by reintervention. Type III events developed in 22.7% (5/22), confined to multi-stent constructs (45.5% vs. 0%; P = 0.035). Primary patency was 81.8% (18/22) at a median 19-month imaging follow-up; secondary patency was 100% after 3 reinterventions. Greater baseline true-lumen stenosis and Yun III morphology predicted composite events. No patient died; the only bowel resection preceded secondary stenting. CONCLUSION: Endovascular therapy for SISMAD fails in characteristic, morphology-dependent patterns. The proposed three-type classification is exploratory and requires validation in larger cohorts.

We analyzed device- and procedure-related failure modes in a 17-year single-center cohort. METHODS: We reviewed 117 consecutive patients with SISMAD (2008-2025).

title: Use of smart glasses for ultrasound-guided central venous catheterization in adults: a randomized clinical trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Head-mounted displays can be integrated with ultrasonography to overlay the image in the operator's field of view, improving hand-eye coordination during invasive procedures. The clinical efficacy of smart glasses for central venous catheterization (CVC) remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate whether using smart glasses can improve efficiency compared to conventional ultrasound-guided CVC. METHODS: This prospective, single-blinded, controlled study enrolled adult patients who underwent elective surgery requiring CVC. Patients were assigned to either the ultrasound screen (control) or smart glasses group using stratified randomization according to operator qualification. The primary outcome was the overall CVC procedural time. Secondary outcomes included ultrasound scanning and venous access time, number of needle redirections and probe repositionings, procedural success and complication rates. RESULTS: In total, 124 patients were analyzed. The overall procedural time was significantly reduced in the smart glasses group compared to that in the control group (158 [140, 189] s vs. 134 [117,150] s; median difference, 26.0 s; 95% CI, [16.0-37.0] s, P < 0.001). Specifically, the ultrasound scanning time (median difference, 3.0 s, P = 0.004), venous access time (median difference, 2.0 s, P = 0.013), number of needle redirections (median difference, 1.0, P = 0.003) and probe repositionings (median difference, 0.0, P = 0.005) were significantly reduced in the smart glasses group compared to those in the control group. However, the success and complication rates were comparable between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Smart glasses modestly improved procedural efficiency in ultrasound-guided CVC, potientially for novices, without improving success or complication rates. Larger-sample studies with more diverse operators and patients are warranted. title: AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy under superior vena cava filter protection for acute upper extremity deep vein thrombosis in patients with cancer: a single-center, retrospective analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The incidence of upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT) is increasing, and percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy (PMT) is receiving more attention as a treatment option. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and clinical outcomes of PMT combined with superior vena cava (SVC) filter protection in cancer patients with acute UEDVT. METHODS: This study included all patients with acute UEDVT who underwent treatment with an 8-Fr AngioJet thrombectomy system (Boston Scientific) under the protection of a retrievable SVC filter between January 1, 2020, and October 1, 2025. The evaluation indicators included technical success rate (defined as a thrombus clearance rate >80%), intraoperative adverse events, degree of limb swelling relief, incidence of pulmonary embolism, and thrombus recurrence during follow-up. RESULTS: A total of 19 patients (10 female; mean age 60.84 ± 11.30 years) were included. All patients had secondary UEDVT and a history of malignant tumors, with 14 cases (73.7%) having a history of central venous catheterization. All procedures achieved technical success, with no severe adverse events such as major bleeding occurring intraoperatively, nor were there any new symptomatic pulmonary embolisms. The average circumference of the affected limb 10 cm above the elbow before surgery was 29.83 ± 2.20 cm, which decreased to 26.98 ± 2.0 cm on the second postoperative day. During the 6-month follow-up, one patient with advanced lung cancer developed swelling of the upper limb on postoperative day 136, confirmed by ultrasound to be a recurrence of deep vein thrombosis; another patient was found to have an asymptomatic mural thrombus on ultrasound examination on postoperative day 28. CONCLUSION: PMT with the 8-Fr AngioJet system and SVC filter protection appears to be a safe and effective treatment option for cancer patients with acute UEDVT.

This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and clinical outcomes of PMT combined with superior vena cava (SVC) filter protection in cancer patients with acute UEDVT. METHODS: This study included all patients with acute UEDVT who underwent treatment with an 8-Fr AngioJet thrombectomy system (Boston Scientific) under the protection of a retrievable SVC filter between January 1, 2020, and October 1, 2025.

title: Hemodynamic Analysis of Modified Splenic Arteriovenous Shunt in Pancreas Transplantation.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a modified splenic arteriovenous shunt technique in pancreas transplantation through intraoperative hemodynamic monitoring and postoperative follow-up. METHODS: A total of 12 patients undergoing simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplantation were enrolled. Under three consecutive intraoperative states (spleen preserved, splenic arteriovenous clamped, and splenic arteriovenous shunt created), color Doppler ultrasound was used to measure peak systolic velocity (PS) and volumetric flow (VF) of the splenic artery and vein at the same point in the distal pancreatic tail, while portal venous pressure was recorded using an intravascular pressure transducer. Postoperative graft function, thrombotic events, and complications were regularly followed up. RESULTS: Compared with the spleen-preserved state, the clamped state showed significant reductions in splenic arterial PS and VF (15.24 ± 4.43 cm/s, 16.62 ± 6.84 mL/min) and splenic venous PS and VF (16.31 ± 3.82 cm/s, 60.32 ± 16.07 mL/min) (P < 0.001). In the shunt state, splenic arterial (54.47 ± 3.45 cm/s, 157.39 ± 11.24 mL/min) and venous (49.27 ± 6.61 cm/s, 177.89 ± 14.15 mL/min) flow parameters showed no significant differences compared with the spleen-preserved state (P > 0.05), but were significantly higher than those in the clamped state (P < 0.001). Portal venous pressure showed no significant differences among the three states (P > 0.05). At a median follow-up of 5 months, no graft thrombosis, pancreatitis, or gastrointestinal bleeding was observed, and patient and graft survival rates were both 100% at the last follow-up. Glycated hemoglobin decreased from 7.37% ± 0.68% preoperatively to 5.81% ± 0.32% (P < 0.005), and left ventricular ejection fraction increased from 59.50% ± 3.23% to 67.33% ± 2.84% (P < 0.005). CONCLUSION: The modified splenic arteriovenous shunt maintains physiological perfusion of the pancreatic allograft without elevating portal venous pressure, and may mitigate the hypoperfusion and blood stasis associated with conventional splenic vessel ligation. Based on the short-term results of this study, this modified technique appears safe and feasible, and may contribute to reducing early thrombotic complications after pancreas transplantation.

title: Intended Thrombectomy for Basilar Artery Occlusion with Mild Deficits: Evidence from a Multicenter Prospective Registry.
abstract: P Supplemental material is available for this article. Background The role of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in basilar artery occlusion (BAO) with mild deficits (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score < 10) remains uncertain. Purpose To compare the outcomes of EVT combined with best medical management (BMM) versus BMM alone in individuals with BAO and mild deficits. Materials and Methods Consecutive eligible patients treated at eight stroke centers between September 2023 and March 2025 were enrolled in a prospective registry. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score of 0-2). Secondary outcomes were 90-day excellent outcome (mRS score of 0-1), death, and early neurologic deterioration (END), defined as a four-point or greater increase in NIHSS score within 72 hours. Primary analyses followed an intention-to-treat-like framework with inverse probability weighting (IPW). As-treated and per-protocol sensitivity analyses were used to assess the robustness of the results and the impact of treatment crossover (EVT after END). Results Among 401 participants (mean age, 64.9 years ± 8.9 [SD]; 278 male participants), the median onset-to-arterial-puncture time in the EVT group was 402 minutes (IQR, 271-583 minutes). After multivariable adjustment in the IPW-adjusted data, EVT was associated with higher odds of functional independence (odds ratio [OR], 1.55 [95% CI: 1.17, 2.06]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.48 [95% CI: 1.09, 2.03]) and lower odds of death (OR, 0.65 [95% CI: 0.45, 0.77]) and END (OR, 0.35 [95% CI: 0.20, 0.61]). Subgroup analyses demonstrated EVT-related functional benefit in participants with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not in those with NIHSS scores of 0-5 (for interaction = .02 for functional independence); however, in participants with NIHSS scores of 0-5, EVT was associated with lower odds of END and death. Sensitivity analyses accounting for treatment crossover showed attenuated functional advantage for EVT. Conclusion In participants with BAO and mild deficits, EVT plus BMM was associated with better outcomes than BMM alone; however, functional benefit was observed in those with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not those with NIHSS scores of 0-5. title: A single-cell census of pulmonary endarterectomies tissue across different anatomical regions in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) remains one of potentially curative options for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). The operation can remove proximal thromboembolic materials and their secondary branches. However, the cellular landscape and pathological features across different anatomical regions remain limited understood. METHODS: Ten patients with CTEPH undergoing PEA surgery and six reference distal pulmonary arteries were conducted single-cell transcriptomics to profile the cellular composition of the main and its bifurcate portion. RESULTS: Pronounced muscularised and fibrotic thrombi organisation were presented in the main portion, and the proportion of mononuclear phagocytes was significantly increased. Inflammatory response and pro-inflammatory activity were attributed to CD8+ effector T cells and nature killer cells subsets and a M1-like (high IL1B and TNF, minimal IL6) phenotypic macrophage subcluster. The colander-like lesions were dominant in the bifurcate portion, and the percentage of plasma cells was markedly increased. Immune dysregulation was induced from CD4 naïve T cells, and a downregulation of M2-like macrophage infiltration into the vascular wall. The expression of plasminogen activator, urokinase receptor, urokinase receptor (PLAUR; plasminogen activator) were observed in M2-like (high MRC1 and CD163, virtually no IL1B or TNF) macrophage in bifurcate portion. Notably, one of smooth muscle cells (SMCs) subclusters in the bifurcate portion gained more significantly myofibroblast markers than those in the main portion, and other subclusters remained the function of SMCs. CONCLUSIONS: The regions with colander-like lesions changes had more obviously T cell and macrophages driving immune-inflammatory response and SMCs differentiation, suggesting that combining therapeutic interventions after surgical removal of accessible thrombus may be beneficial. KEY POINTS: This study reveals the comprehensive cellular composition in main/lobar and bifurcate pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) specimens at the single-cell level. The bifurcate regions with colander had more obviously T cell and macrophages driving immune-inflammatory response and smooth muscle cells (SMCs) differentiation, however, the remodelling of distal or micro-vessels still remained.

title: Association between admission D-dimer levels and post-stroke epilepsy risk: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke epilepsy (PSE) is a severe complication following acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet early identification of patients at high risk remains challenging. This study evaluated the association between baseline D-dimer levels and incident PSE within one year after AIS. METHODS: 2 In this secondary analysis of a multicenter retrospective cohort, 21,459 patients with first-ever AIS were included. D-dimer was modeled as a log-transformed continuous variable. Multivariable logistic regression with progressive adjustment, restricted cubic spline analysis, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Internal validation was conducted using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: The median baseline D-dimer level was 0.92 mg/L (IQR 0.65-1.49). PSE occurred in 936 patients (4.36%). After full adjustment, each doubling of D-dimer was associated with a 3.3-fold increase in PSE odds (OR 3.33, 95% CI 2.94-3.78). The association remained consistent in sensitivity analyses excluding patients with deep vein thrombosis (OR 3.86, 95% CI 3.37-4.43), atrial fibrillation (OR 3.50, 95% CI 3.04-4.04), or extreme D-dimer values (OR 3.41, 95% CI 2.99-3.91). A non-linear relationship was observed, with PSE risk rising more steeply at higher D-dimer levels. The C-statistic for the fully adjusted model was 0.968. CONCLUSION: Elevated baseline D-dimer levels were independently associated with an increased risk of PSE within one year after AIS. As a routinely available biomarker, D-dimer may inform risk assessment in acute stroke units; however, external validation in independent cohorts with prospective PSE ascertainment is required before clinical implementation.

title: Integrated Analysis of Serotonin-Related Biomarkers in Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Based on Machine Learning and Single-Cell Sequencing Data.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Serotonin, as an important neurotransmitter and signaling molecule, can affect thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) by regulating vascular cell proliferation, angiogenesis, and immune status. This research aimed to conduct a comprehensive analysis to pinpoint serotonin-related biomarkers in TAA and to elucidate their potential molecular mechanisms.Biomarkers were selected and validated through differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), machine learning algorithms, and expression verification. Moreover, the constructed nomogram, enrichment analysis, immune infiltration analysis, and compound prediction validated the regulatory roles of the biomarkers in TAA. The single-cell dataset was analyzed to determine key cells and perform pseudo-time analysis. Simulated knockout of biomarkers was performed to determine their underlying functions and related pathways. Finally, reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) was employed to confirm the expression levels of the biomarkers.Overall, two biomarkers (CD300A and CLU) were determined to be associated with serotonin in TAA. The nomogram showed good performance in predicting TAA risk. These biomarkers were significantly enriched in the hematopoietic cell lineage and natural killer (NK) cell mediated cytotoxicity. Biomarker expression was significantly correlated with the infiltration proportions of M2 macrophages and neutrophils. The biomarkers were stably bound to tetrachlorodibenzodioxin and bisphenol A. Moreover, pseudo-time analysis demonstrated a notable correlation between biomarker expression and the differentiation status of monocytes/macrophages/dendritic cells (MonoMac/DC). Genes perturbed by knockout were enriched in the pyrimidine metabolism and RIG-I-like receptor signaling pathway. Finally, RT-qPCR validated that CLU was downregulated and CD300A was upregulated in the TAA group.Biomarkers (CD300A and CLU) associated with serotonin in TAA were identified, with their expression trends validated by RT-qPCR. This work provides novel bioinformatic insights, and direct functional experiments are required to support future therapeutic development for TAA.

title: Transcatheter Electrosurgical Aortic Septotomy Across the Spectrum of Type B Aortic Dissection: Feasibility, Technical Lessons, and Bailout Strategies.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter electrosurgical aortic septotomy (TEAS) has been introduced to optimise luminal geometry during endovascular repair of complex type B aortic dissection (TBAD), but data across dissection phases and on complication management remain limited. This study reports early outcomes, quantitative common lumen creation, and bailout strategies from a consecutive single centre experience. METHOD: Eight consecutive patients underwent TEAS, between December 2024 and January 2026, as an adjunct to thoracic endovascular aortic repair or physician modified fenestrated endograft for acute, subacute, or chronic TBAD, including post-type A repair and genetic aortopathy. Pre-procedural and follow up computed tomography angiography (CTA) quantified true lumen and common lumen cross sectional area. Septotomy technical success, peri-operative outcomes, complications, and early follow up were assessed. RESULTS: 2 2 The mean age was 51.1 ± 17 years; five were men. Two patients were acute, two subacute, and four chronic; two had Marfan syndrome, both redo cases after previous open repair. Septotomy technical success was 100%. The median cross sectional area increased from 174.5 mm(pre-procedural true lumen) to 1 007 mm(follow up CTA common lumen) after TEAS (5.3 fold increase). There were no 30 day, in hospital, or aortic related deaths. Three major procedure related complications (38%) occurred, all in non-acute cases and all managed endovascularly: one iliac lamellar dislodgement requiring kissing stents, one external iliac rupture treated with stent grafting, and one delayed superior mesenteric artery occlusion managed with stenting. All acute cases were uneventful. Median clinical follow up was 32 days (range 22 - 308) and median imaging follow up was 20 days (range 2 - 265), with no late deaths, no aortic re-interventions, and no aneurysmal dilatation of the non-stented TEAS treated segment. CONCLUSION: TEAS may be considered across acute, subacute, and chronic TBAD, including redo and connective tissue disease cases, enabling reproducible common lumen creation and landing zone optimisation. All complications were recognised and managed endovascularly and were observed only in non-acute dissections, although the sample size precluded meaningful assessment of any relationship between dissection phase and technical risk. These findings support TEAS as a feasible adjunct in carefully selected complex dissections, offer practical principles for safe adoption, and reflect an early experience that may be influenced by the learning curve of this technically demanding procedure.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analyses Identify CCR2-Dependent Monocyte-Smooth Muscle Cell Crosstalk in Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Aortic aneurysm (AA) involves inflammatory recruitment and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) remodeling, but the cellular contribution of candidate chemokine receptors remains unclear. We prioritized reproducible AA-associated genes, localized their cellular sources, and tested whether monocyte CCR2 influences human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs). METHODS: Differentially expressed genes shared by GSE57691 and GSE7084 underwent enrichment, protein-protein interaction, regulatory-network, and drug-gene analyses. Hub genes were assessed in GSE9106 and localized in GSE166676 single-cell RNA-sequencing data. CCR2-silenced THP-1 monocytic cells were indirectly co-cultured with HASMCs. CCR2 knockdown was verified by quantitative PCR; HASMC remodeling-related proteins and 24-h scratch-wound closure were evaluated. RESULTS: p p p We identified 107 common upregulated genes and ten immune-related hubs. CCR2 was monocyte-enriched and higher in AA cells overall (= 0.00799) and AA monocytes (= 0.00440). THP-1 co-culture increased COL3A1 and SPP1, decreased α-SMA and TPM, and increased HASMC wound closure. CCR2 silencing partially reversed these changes and decreased wound closure versus siNC-THP-1 cells (< 0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Multi-omic evidence and non-contact co-culture support CCR2-dependent monocyte-HASMC paracrine crosstalk in AA-associated remodeling. The responsible mediators and in vivo relevance require further study.

title: Perioperative Predictors and Temporal Trajectories of Postoperative Cognitive Decline After Carotid Endarterectomy: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Carotid artery stenosis is a well-established risk factor for vascular cognitive impairment. Although carotid endarterectomy (CEA) reduces the risk of ischemic stroke, its effect on cognitive function remains uncertain. Most previous studies have relied on mean changes in cognitive scores and have not defined postoperative cognitive decline using patient-level thresholds for the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Moreover, few studies have integrated perioperative variables across baseline, intraoperative, and postoperative domains to examine heterogeneity in cognitive outcomes. We therefore defined postoperative cognitive decline using threshold-based MoCA changes and prospectively evaluated perioperative factors associated with distinct cognitive outcomes after CEA. METHODS: We prospectively enrolled older patients undergoing elective CEA under general anesthesia. Of 183 patients screened, 162 were ultimately enrolled and analyzed. All patients were managed according to standardized anesthetic and surgical protocols. Preoperative clinical, laboratory, and imaging variables, intraoperative hemodynamic parameters, and postoperative clinical indicators were collected. The primary outcome was cognitive decline at discharge, defined as a decrease of ≥2 points from baseline in the MoCA score. The secondary outcome was cognitive decline at 30 days, defined as a ≥3-point decrease in the telephone MoCA (t-MoCA) score relative to the corresponding baseline domains. RESULTS: Among the 162 enrolled patients, preoperative triglyceride level, preoperative cerebral hypoperfusion volume, surgical laterality, intraoperative mean arterial pressure (MAP) decline, and visual analogue scale (VAS) on postoperative day 1 were independently associated with early postoperative cognitive decline. A prediction model incorporating these five factors achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.752 (95% CI: 0.670-0.835) for cognitive decline before discharge. For 30-day cognitive decline, the model demonstrated an AUC of 0.717 (95% CI: 0.606-0.828). All patients with complete 30-day follow-up were stratified into four cognitive trajectory subtypes, and their longitudinal cognitive changes were visualized using a Sankey diagram. CONCLUSIONS: A perioperative model incorporating metabolic, cerebral perfusion, surgical, hemodynamic, and pain-related variables may help identify patients at increased risk of cognitive decline after CEA. The trajectory analysis further reveals heterogeneous postoperative cognitive patterns, including transient, delayed, and persistent decline. These findings support individualized perioperative risk assessment and structured cognitive follow-up. However, no internal or external validation was performed, and further testing is required in larger multicenter cohorts.

title: [Effects of digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation on clinical outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement].
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effects of digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation on clinical outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). This study has been registered with the U.S. National Library of Medicine Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier NCT02803294. METHODS: Data from 1012 patients who underwent TAVR at the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, between March 2013 and January 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients receiving conventional rehabilitation were assigned to the control group, whereas those receiving a digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation program, comprising preoperative screening and functional preparation, intraoperative eligibility assessment, postoperative stepwise rehabilitation management, and intelligent home-based rehabilitation, were assigned to the observation group. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline confounding. Postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) stay and hospital stay, the incidence of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular adverse events at 30 days, 1 year, and 2 years after TAVR, and functional outcomes, including the five-meter walking test, six-minute walking test, and Katz index, were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: vs P vs P P P After propensity score matching, 251 patients were included in each group. Compared with the control group, the observation group had shorter postoperative ICU stays [0 (0, 1) h. 0 (0, 0) h,<0.01] and postoperative hospital stays [8 (7, 11) d. 3 (1, 7) d,<0.01]. No apparent increase in the incidence of adverse events was observed in the observation group at 30 days, 1 year, or 2 years after TAVR. The time required to complete the five-meter walking test was shorter in the observation group than in the control group at 30 days, 1 year, and 2 years after TAVR (all<0.01). Results of six-minute walking test and Katz index showed no significant differences between the groups (both>0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation may shorten hospital stay and improve selected functional outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR without increase in postoperative cardiovascular and cerebrovascular adverse events.

title: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae RkMsn4, a zinc finger transcription factor, regulates carotenoid and lipid metabolism to enhance tolerance to environmental stress in.
abstract: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Red yeasts serve as indispensable microbial resources for the production of carotenoids and lipids; however, environmental stress factors often limit their performance during industrial fermentation. The zinc-finger transcription factors Msn2/Msn4 act as central regulators of stress responses in yeasts. However, researchers have not yet systematically elucidated the similarities and differences in the mechanisms underlying the regulatory effects of Msn2/Msn4 under different stress conditions. In this study, we compared the shared and stress-specific regulatory functions of RkMsn4 inYM25235 under conditions of glucose starvation, 15 °C low temperature, and 4% NaCl salt stress. RkMsn4 contributed to the activity of the oxidative defense systems, including antioxidant enzymes, carotenoids, and glutathione, and the remodeling of membrane lipids, including phospholipids and unsaturated fatty acids (UFAs) across all three stress conditions. Additionally, RkMsn4 regulated stress-specific metabolic regulation by modulating branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) and aromatic amino acid (AAA) metabolism under glucose starvation conditions and promoting the utilization of exogenous sucrose and fructose under salt stress. By conducting weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), we identified candidate genes potentially associated with carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide practical insights for improving tolerance to stress and metabolic productivity of red yeasts in industrial bioprocesses.IMPORTANCERed yeasts are important microorganisms for the production of carotenoids and lipids, but their performance is often limited by environmental stress. Understanding how red yeasts respond to environmental stress is crucial for advancing their application in industrial fermentation. This study reveals the stress response mechanisms mediated by the transcription factor RkMsn4 inYM25235 under glucose starvation, low temperature, and salt stress, as well as its regulatory role in carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide valuable insights for enhancing the stress resistance and productivity of red yeasts in industrial applications.

title: Obesity-Related Traits Partially Mediate the Impact of Obstructive Sleep Apnea on the Risk of Venous Thromboembolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although observational studies have suggested an association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and thromboembolism, causal evidence remains to be established. METHODS: Linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC) was used to evaluate the genetic correlations between OSA and thromboembolism. Based on the results of LDSC, two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses were performed to investigate the causal relationships between OSA and thromboembolism traits, such as venous thromboembolism (VTE), pulmonary embolism (PE), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and phlebitis and thrombophlebitis (not including DVT) (PT), including reverse associations. Four common MR methods, in addition to Bayesian weighted MR analysis, were applied to evaluate causality. Multivariable analyses were conducted after adjustment for potential confounders, including sedentary behaviors (e.g., driving, computer use, and television watching), smoking, and alcohol consumption. Mediation analysis was performed to assess the mediating role of obesity-related traits. RESULTS: LDSC identified genetic correlations between OSA and thromboembolic subtypes (VTE, PE, and PT). Univariate MR indicated that OSA genetically predicted an increased risk of VTE, PE, and PT, with no evidence of significant reverse causality. After adjusting for confounders, OSA remained significantly associated with these traits. Mediation analyses revealed that the effect of OSA on thromboembolism was partially mediated by obesity-related traits. CONCLUSION: This study identified a positive causal association between OSA and specific thromboembolic subtypes, with no evidence of reverse causality. Obesity may partially mediate the effect of OSA on thromboembolism.

title: Multicomponent Pulmonary Rehabilitation for Prolonged Mechanical Ventilation in Patients 80 Years of Age or Older: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Older patients receiving prolonged mechanical ventilation (MV) have a low likelihood of successful ventilator liberation and remain at risk of infectious complications and death. RESEARCH QUESTION: In patients ≥ 80 years of age receiving prolonged MV, does a multicomponent pulmonary rehabilitation program increase successful weaning? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: This single-center, assessor-masked randomized controlled trial was conducted at Chinese PLA General Hospital. Patients ≥ 80 years of age receiving prolonged MV were randomized to multicomponent pulmonary rehabilitation or standard rehabilitation. The primary outcome was successful weaning. Secondary outcomes were oxygen saturation while not receiving MV, diaphragm thickening fraction, cough ability, muscle strength, and the incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) assessed at 30, 60, and 90 days. Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) was assessed at day 90 or when participation ended. RESULTS: The intention-to-treat analysis included 75 patients in each group. Among patients who received the multicomponent pulmonary rehabilitation program, 45.3% achieved successful weaning, compared with 12.0% among patients receiving standard rehabilitation (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 5.11; 95% CI, 2.46-11.23; P < .001). No significant difference was found in the incidence of DVT between the 2 groups. The intervention group showed higher odds of meeting the prespecified improvement criteria for oxygen saturation, diaphragm thickening fraction, cough strength, and muscle strength at 30, 60, and 90 days, whereas VAP incidence was lower at days 60 and 90. The all-cause mortality rate at 90 days was 2.7% (2/75) in the trial group and 4.0% (3/75) in the control group (P = 1.000). The per-protocol analysis yielded similar results. The Fine-Gray competing risk analysis yielded a subdistribution HR of 4.45 (95% CI, 2.11-9.36; P < .001). INTERPRETATION: Our results show that in patients ≥ 80 years of age receiving prolonged MV, the multicomponent pulmonary rehabilitation program improved physiologic recovery and significantly increased successful weaning. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry; No.: ChiCTR2100050342; URL: www.chictr.org.cn.

title: Deciphering ribosomal frameshifting determinants across species with a semi-supervised hybrid learning framework.
abstract: Programmed ribosomal frameshifting (PRF) is a conserved translational recoding mechanism that expands proteome diversity and regulates important biological processes across viruses, prokaryotes, and eukaryotes. However, existing predictors are often limited by their reliance on extensive annotated data, poor performance in non-model organisms, and restricted applicability across species or frameshift types. Here, we present FScanpy, a hybrid machine-learning model integrating histogram-based gradient boosting (HistGB) and a bidirectional long short-term memory-convolutional neural network (BiLSTM-CNN) architecture for cross-species PRF prediction. The model integrates short-range codon-position features associated with ribosomal pausing and long-range sequence contexts that reflect structural constraints around candidate shift sites. Using semi-supervised learning on 8 049 candidate sequences, FScanpy reduces reliance on manual annotation and improves model generalization. Across multiple datasets, it achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.951, and it also performed well on euplotid protists (AUC=0.877), supporting its utility in non-model systems with non-canonical recoding patterns. Feature interpretation further showed that AAA and GGG motifs, together with mRNA secondary-structure stability, as major determinants across datasets, highlighting conserved features of PRF from viruses to eukaryotes. These insights not only validate the model's accuracy but also deepen understanding of PRF's conserved biological roles. FScanpy establishes a novel and effective computational framework for PRF analysis by resolving challenges in feature representation and species generalizability, enabling the study of frameshifting sites and accelerating discovery of evolutionarily divergent recoding events.

Here, we present FScanpy, a hybrid machine-learning model integrating histogram-based gradient boosting (HistGB) and a bidirectional long short-term memory-convolutional neural network (BiLSTM-CNN) architecture for cross-species PRF prediction.

title: TRPV4 is Associated with a Marfan Syndrome-Related Mechanosensitive Gene Program in Aortic Smooth Muscle Cells.
abstract: Marfan syndrome (MFS) aortopathy involves extracellular matrix disruption, altered mechanical cues, and maladaptive vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) remodeling. However, the mechanosensitive regulators associated with MFS-related VSMC dysfunction remain unclear. This study aimed to identify and validate mechanosensitive candidate genes in MFS aortopathy. Public VSMC transcriptomic data from GSE128101 were re-analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Protein-protein interaction analysis, functional enrichment, and minimum redundancy maximum relevance analysis were used to prioritize mechanosensitive candidates. Candidate genes were examined in independent MFS-related datasets and validated by qRT-PCR in primary aortic medial VSMCs from MFS patients and donor controls. TRPV4 localization was assessed by immunofluorescence. TRPV4 function was evaluated in primary human aortic smooth muscle cells using overexpression and siRNA-mediated knockdown, followed by proliferation, wound-closure, inflammatory cytokine, and NF-κB pathway assays. A total of 436 DEGs were identified in MFS-derived aortic VSMCs. Functional analyses highlighted extracellular matrix remodeling, mechanotransduction-related, inflammatory, and cytoskeleton-associated pathways. TRPV4 was the top-ranked mechanosensitive candidate, with TRPM5 also identified as an overlapping candidate. qRT-PCR confirmed increased TRPV4 and TRPM5 expression in MFS-derived VSMCs. MFS-derived VSMCs also showed elevated inflammatory gene expression and enhanced membrane-associated TRPV4 localization. In vitro, TRPV4 overexpression promoted proliferation, wound closure, inflammatory cytokine secretion, and NF-κB pathway phosphorylation, whereas TRPV4 knockdown showed opposite effects. These exploratory findings identify TRPV4 as a leading mechanosensitive candidate associated with MFS-related VSMC remodeling and inflammatory activation. Larger cohorts, MFS-specific models, and direct mechanistic assays are required to determine its biomarker or therapeutic relevance.

title: Hemodynamic Insights Into an Accessory Splenic Artery Aneurysm Arising From the Superior Mesenteric Artery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Splenic artery variations involve anomalies in origin, course, and branching. Notably, the accessory splenic artery (ASA) is a rare independent, ectopic aberrant duplication outside the celiac trunk, making its comprehension crucial for safety during endovascular interventions. CASE SUMMARY: This case report describes a 34-year-old woman with a rare splenic artery duplication, consisting of a primary splenic artery normally originating from the celiac trunk and an ASA arising from the superior mesenteric artery that harbored a distal saccular aneurysm. DISCUSSION: An ASA originating from the superior mesenteric artery and associated with aneurysm formation is an extremely rare anatomical variation. Hemodynamic evaluations based on computational fluid dynamics simulation indicated that the unique vascular configuration of this aberrant artery may predispose the aneurysm to an elevated risk of rupture. TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This type of accessory splenic artery originating from the superior mesenteric artery is reported here for the first time.
